…Lauds NIMC for recording nearly 140m enrolment

By Emmanuel Elebeke

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has said the Federal Government is targeting 95 per cent National Identification Number (NIN) enrolment coverage by December 2026.

Tinubu disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja at the 8th National Identity Day celebration. He was represented at the event by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila.

The President said the Federal Government was building the digital infrastructure required to leverage Nigeria’s identity system for economic growth.

He said the theme of the celebration underscored the importance of linking the country’s digital ecosystem with its digital economy and broader economic development.

“Nigeria’s digital ecosystem must power Nigeria’s digital economy and Nigeria’s digital economy must help power Africa’s economy. Our identity infrastructure will be a critical component of this ambition,” he said.

Tinubu said the government was working towards an ecosystem in which trusted digital identity would support digital commerce, financial services, social protection, healthcare, education and mobility.

He also disclosed that the government was accelerating the development of a Sovereign Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) as a trust layer within its broader Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) architecture.

According to him, the initiative would strengthen the foundations required for secure digital signatures, trusted electronic documents, encrypted transactions and secure government communications.

He said the system would enable businesses to transact digitally with greater confidence while allowing government documents to be authenticated without cumbersome physical processes.

Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to developing a robust DPI to improve access to public services, describing it as critical to healthcare, education and financial inclusion.

He commended the Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC), Engr. Dr Abisoye Coker-Odusote, for her leadership of the commission.

In his goodwill message, the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, said identity management was central to economic growth, national security and social inclusion.

Tunji-Ojo said Tinubu’s assent to the NIMC Act 2026 provided what he described as a stronger legal foundation for digital identity management and the country’s digital economy.

He said a modern state needed reliable population data to improve the planning and delivery of public services, including education, healthcare and social interventions.

The minister commended Coker-Odusote for what he described as innovations and a citizen-focused approach at NIMC.

He, however, urged the commission to expand access to NIN enrolment for Nigerians in the diaspora and accelerate the development of trusted PKI and DPI systems for secure authentication.

Tunji-Ojo also urged Nigerians to enrol for NIN and protect their identity credentials, saying, “Your identity is your digital footprint.”

The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, said trusted identity management was increasingly important to education planning and access.

Alausa said the ministry was deploying NIN through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI), with the identification number serving as the anchor for cleaning up the education database of more than 75 million students from basic to tertiary levels.

He said NIN had become mandatory for JAMB registration and other examinations as part of efforts to curb malpractice, eliminate multiple identities and improve the accuracy of student records.

According to him, integration with NIMC had enabled more than 800,000 students to access financing through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND).

Alausa also commended NIMC for extending enrolment to 8,809 wards, saying the initiative would improve access to identity registration for school-age children.

Earlier, Coker-Odusote said the national identity database had grown from about 80 million NINs at the inception of the current administration to nearly 140 million.

She said the national identity infrastructure now had the capacity to accommodate 250 million records.

According to her, NIMC launched the Ward-Level Enrolment Drive in February 2026, taking free NIN registration to all 8,809 wards.

She added that more than 5,000 enrolment agents had been trained to improve access for persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.

Coker-Odusote also said NIMC unveiled the NINAuth application on October 30, 2025, describing it as a consent-based, citizen-controlled authentication service.

She added that the commission had relaunched the General Multipurpose Card (GMPC) for identity verification, financial transactions and direct government-to-people services.

The NIMC DG also cited the enactment of the NIMC Act 2026, which she said strengthened data protection, expanded the mandatory use of NIN and increased penalties for identity-related offences.

She said the NIN system now supports economic activities, with more than 173 private companies, 30 state governments and 14 public institutions licensed as enrolment partners.

According to her, NIN has also served as the Tax ID for individuals since January 1, 2026, while more than 800,000 students have accessed education financing through NELFUND following the integration of the identity system.

Coker-Odusote said integration with the Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Immigration Service, Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Nigeria Revenue Service and National Population Commission was also strengthening national security and service delivery.

The event was attended by the ministers of Interior, Education, and Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy.

content:
Teenage brothers Olly and Seb Fisher are closing in on their international debuts with Uganda after being invited to train with the country’s youth national teams.

In a report by BBC Sport on Wednesday, the Partick Thistle youngsters are eligible to represent Uganda through their mother, Kate, who was born in the East African country.

Olly, 18, is a goalkeeper, while 16-year-old Seb is a striker. Both have been training with Uganda’s Under-20 and Under-17 teams respectively and say they have embraced the opportunity.

The brothers first became aware of Uganda’s interest about six months ago after their father had a conversation with a football consultant at a game in Nigeria.

They were subsequently invited to training camps in August and spent a week in Jinja, eastern Uganda.

Olly said the call-up came as a surprise.

“A real mixture of emotions. I was quite shocked. I didn’t really think that this was a possibility but I was honoured to be asked to represent Uganda. I thought it was a real big opportunity.”

Seb, who has also been impressed by the experience, said he initially struggled to believe the opportunity was real.

“I couldn’t believe it. It’s one of those things you look at and you’re shocked. You can’t believe it. Most other people couldn’t as well.”

The brothers have a strong family connection to Uganda. Their grandparents lived in the country for several years after their grandfather moved there to teach, while their mother was born there.

“My gran and grandad lived out here for, I think, four or five years. My grandfather came out here to teach in a school then my mum was born here. So, it’s a bit of a strange one,” Olly said.

‘History in the making’

Uganda Under-20 head coach and former Hearts and Ghana midfielder Laryea Kingston has also welcomed the brothers into the setup.

Seb said Kingston told them they could become the first white players to represent Uganda, although that historical claim has not been independently established.

“Coach Kingston was saying we’d be the first white boys to play for Uganda, which would be history in the making. It is very special,” Seb said.

Olly added:

“It’s never been done before, so definitely it is very special.”

The brothers said they have quickly settled into the squad, with their new teammates helping them adapt to the environment.

“Everyone has been brilliant, welcoming, really great. The other boys have been brand new with us,” Seb said.

Some of their teammates also come from the same area where their mother was born, giving the brothers an additional connection to the country.

International ambitions

The brothers are hoping their involvement with Uganda will lead to competitive international appearances.

Olly hopes to be involved if Uganda qualify for next year’s Under-20 Africa Cup of Nations, while Seb could be in contention for the Under-17 squad for the November World Cup in Qatar.

For Seb, the experience is also an opportunity to develop as a player.

“That’s what you want as a footballer, being in an international environment. It makes you a better player and hopefully it does for the two of us, and I think it will, and benefit us very much going back to Scotland playing at Thistle.”

The brothers are expected to return to Scotland soon, where they will continue combining their football commitments with education at Partick Thistle, while remaining hopeful of further opportunities with Uganda.

title: King’s College crisis deepens over alleged police assault
description:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young



Fresh crisis has erupted at King’s College, Lagos, after the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria (ASCSN) accused the police and members of the King’s College Old Boys Association (KCOBA) of invading the school premises and assaulting workers and parents.
content:
By Victor Ahiuma-Young

Fresh crisis has erupted at King’s College, Lagos, after the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria (ASCSN) accused the police and members of the King’s College Old Boys Association (KCOBA) of invading the school premises and assaulting workers and parents.

ASCSN alleged that the police operation, which it said was led by the Lagos State Commissioner of Police, involved the forceful opening of the school gates, gunshots being fired into the air, physical assaults on civil servants and the arrest of a child of a protesting parent.

The union said the incident occurred amid ongoing discussions involving the Federal Ministry of Education, the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) and ASCSN over the proposed concession of the historic institution.

In a statement, ASCSN National President and General-Secretary, Shehu Mohammed and Joshua Apebo, respectively, condemned what they described as an alleged violent invasion of the school.

The union said the incident occurred at about 8 a.m. on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, alleging that armed policemen stormed the school premises and used a generating set to force open the padlocked gates.

According to ASCSN, gunshots were fired into the air during the operation, while some civil servants were allegedly assaulted and several workers sustained injuries.

The union also alleged that a child of a protesting parent was arrested during the incident.

ASCSN claimed the operation was carried out to grant KCOBA access to the school for a press engagement, describing the development as an escalation of the dispute over the proposed concession.

The union said the incident was particularly concerning because it occurred less than 24 hours after a meeting involving the Minister of Education, TUC and ASCSN to discuss the concession proposal.

“At the very moment when dialogue and lawful processes were underway, state security forces were deployed to sabotage trust, undermine negotiations, and intimidate workers,” the union alleged.

ASCSN also accused KCOBA of using the police to intimidate civil servants who, according to the union, were exercising their right to oppose what it described as the proposed commercialisation of the institution.

The union called on the Inspector-General of Police to withdraw police personnel from the school, arguing that the police should not be used to interfere in the dispute.

ASCSN said the incident had further damaged its confidence in KCOBA’s engagement with labour and could affect the implementation of agreements reached between the Federal Ministry of Education, TUC and the union.

It commended its members and parents who participated in the protest, saying it remained committed to defending public education and the rights of its members.

The union warned that continued use of force instead of dialogue would lead to further lawful action by its members.

The allegations by ASCSN could not be independently verified at the time of filing this report.

content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

The World Health Organization (WHO) has urged African countries to prioritise patient safety in the treatment of noncommunicable diseases (NCDs), warning that patients face risks of avoidable harm at different stages of care.

The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, made the call in a message marking the 2026 World Patient Safety Day, themed, “Safe care for noncommunicable diseases,” with the slogan, “Safe care for life!”

Janabi said people living with diabetes, cancer, heart disease and chronic respiratory conditions often require long-term consultations, tests, medications, referrals and treatment, exposing them to risks including delayed diagnosis, medication errors, adverse drug interactions, poor follow-up and communication gaps.

He noted that NCDs caused at least 43 million deaths globally in 2021 and accounted for 37 per cent of all deaths in the WHO African Region in 2019, compared with 24 per cent in 2000.

According to him, nearly two-thirds of NCD deaths in the region were premature, compared with 41.7 per cent globally.

He added that NCDs remained a major cause of long-term disability and loss of function.

Janabi said risks could arise throughout a patient’s health journey, including diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, palliative care and self-management, and could be compounded by stigma, discrimination and limited access to essential medicines and health technologies.

He stressed that efforts to expand access to NCD services must be accompanied by measures to improve the quality and safety of care.

“Strong primary healthcare systems are essential for ensuring continuity of care, early identification of health problems and effective coordination between different levels of the health system,” he said.

Janabi urged health workers to have access to practical guidance, reliable supplies, adequate training and supportive working environments where errors could be reported and used to improve services without fear of blame.

He said countries in the African Region were expanding integrated NCD services through approaches such as WHO PEN at the primary healthcare level and PEN-Plus at first-level referral facilities.

According to him, the approaches bring diagnosis, treatment and long-term care closer to communities while promoting safer care through evidence-based treatment protocols, clear referral pathways and regular monitoring.

The WHO official also called for greater involvement of people living with NCDs in efforts to improve patient safety, saying their experiences could help identify gaps in healthcare delivery.

“Listening to their experience, communicating clearly and involving them in decisions can prevent harm and improve treatment outcomes,” he said.

He urged health professionals to follow evidence-based protocols and communicate openly with patients and colleagues.

Janabi also encouraged patients and their families to ask questions and raise concerns whenever they were unclear about their care.

“Every person should be protected from avoidable harm throughout their health journey.

“Together, we can reduce avoidable harm and build health services that earn and sustain the trust of the people they serve,” he said.

content:
The Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, has mourned the death of veteran Nollywood actor and cultural icon, Oludotun Baiyewu Jacobs, popularly known as Olu Jacobs, who died on Wednesday at the age of 84.

Musawa described the death of the celebrated actor as a monumental loss to Nigeria and the country’s creative industry, saying Jacobs’ contribution to the arts spanned more than five decades.

In a statement issued by her Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Nneka Anibeze, in Abuja on Wednesday, the minister described Jacobs as “a national institution” and one of the pillars of Nigeria’s entertainment industry.

She said, “Olu Jacobs was not just an actor; he was a national institution. He was one of the most important pillars of Nigeria’s entertainment industry and one of Africa’s greatest actors.

“For over five decades, his voice, his presence and his craft gave life to our stories and gave dignity to our industry.”

Musawa also noted Jacobs’ contribution to developing talents in the creative sector through the Lufodo Academy, which he established with his wife and fellow veteran actress, Joke Silva.

According to her, the academy had trained hundreds of actors, directors and filmmakers who have gone on to play leading roles in Nollywood.

“Through the Lufodo Academy, which has trained hundreds of actors, directors and filmmakers who are now leading Nollywood, and the countless lives he touched, his legacy will continue to live on stage, on screen and in the hearts of millions of Nigerians.

“Nigeria has lost a Lion, but his light will never fade,” she stated.

Jacobs was one of the most prominent figures of Nigeria’s theatre, television and film industries, with a career that spanned several decades and included performances on stage and screen in Nigeria and abroad.

He was trained at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London before establishing himself as a respected actor in British television and theatre productions and later becoming one of the defining figures of Nigeria’s burgeoning film industry.

His career in Nollywood included appearances in numerous acclaimed films and television productions, while his work in theatre and acting education helped shape subsequent generations of Nigerian performers.

Beyond acting, Jacobs and Silva co-founded the Lufodo Group, with interests including film production and performing arts education, as part of their efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s creative industry.

Jacobs’ contribution to the arts was also recognised by the Federal Government, which conferred on him the national honour of Member of the Order of the Federal Republic.

The minister, on behalf of the Federal Government and the creative community, extended condolences to Silva, their children and other members of the Jacobs family.

Musawa also expressed sympathy to Jacobs’ colleagues, friends and the millions of Nigerians who followed his work over the decades.

description:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

The commitment was made at an endorsement rally organised in Akure by the Emerging
content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

Ahead of the 2027 general election, leaders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Ondo State have pledged to work together to mobilise one million votes for President Bola Tinubu.

The commitment was made at an endorsement rally organised in Akure by the Emerging Political Platform (EPP), a support group backing Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Speaking at the event, the Ondo State APC Chairman, Babatunde Kolawole, urged party members to set aside personal interests and work collectively for Tinubu and other APC candidates contesting the Senate, House of Representatives and state House of Assembly elections.

Kolawole described EPP as a support group working for Tinubu’s re-election and said its endorsement reflected its support for the administration.

He said the group had also endorsed APC candidates contesting the National Assembly and state assembly elections.

“It’s about the President. Not just the President, our candidates for Senate, for House of Reps, and for Assembly. We must all do everything as a party to ensure that they come back victorious,” he said.

The APC chairman also dismissed suggestions of a rift between Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa and the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, saying the two leaders were working together for the success of the party and Tinubu.

“When you mention the Minister and the Governor, you make it look as if there’s an issue. They are brothers. The Governor is the Governor, the leader of the party in the state. The Minister is also the Minister, working with Mr. President. They are one,” Kolawole said.

He attributed the state government’s ability to execute projects in sectors including roads, health and education partly to increased federal allocations to the state.

Kolawole also reiterated Aiyedatiwa’s warning against anti-party activities, saying members involved in such activities would face consequences.

“The Governor has said that he has zero tolerance for anti-party activities. He has said that there will be consequences for anybody that is involved in any form of anti-party activities in this state,” he said.

Also speaking, the Director-General of the Asiwaju Mandate Group (AMG) in Ondo State, Olumuyiwa Asagunla, urged APC members to set aside their differences and work together ahead of the election.

Asagunla said the party had concluded its primaries and produced its candidates, adding that members should now focus on mobilising support for Tinubu and other APC candidates.

“This is not the time to say, ‘I’m for Paul, I’m for Apollo.’ We should come under one umbrella and work in unity,” he said.

He urged the party to target at least one million votes for Tinubu in Ondo State, arguing that the APC had an advantage as the dominant political party in the state.

“We should shave all differences and forge ahead so that we can deliver en masse for APC,” Asagunla said.

The President of EPP, Dr Dolapo Fatogun, described the endorsement as a “new beginning” for the APC in the state and said the group was committed to supporting Tinubu and other APC candidates.

Fatogun urged party members to prioritise reconciliation and grassroots mobilisation ahead of the election rather than internal disagreements.

“It signifies a new beginning for the APC. We are all united by the party. That’s APC. We are going nowhere,” he said.

He said the one-million-vote target could be achieved if APC members worked together to mobilise voters who did not participate in previous elections.

“We should stop fighting. We should look directly at our faces and say APC. If APC doesn’t do well, it’s our collective shame,” Fatogun said.

He added that Ondo should aim to surpass the one-million-vote target, citing the state’s representation in the federal cabinet as a factor he believed could strengthen its political mobilisation.

content:
Motorists and commuters were stranded for several hours on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway after a multiple-vehicle crash at Kara Bridge triggered an overnight gridlock on Tuesday.

The crash, which occurred in the early hours of Tuesday, involved seven vehicles and disrupted traffic heading towards Ogun State.

The situation was further worsened by ongoing repair works on the bridge, with the resulting congestion stretching beyond the Long Bridge towards Magboro and extending into Lagos.

Some road users said they spent between six and 14 hours trapped in traffic along the route from Ojota and Berger towards Mowe and Ibafo.

Efforts by some motorists to escape the congestion reportedly created another problem, as several drove against traffic and further obstructed vehicles travelling towards Lagos.

Videos shared on social media on Wednesday captured frustrated commuters recounting their experiences after spending hours in the gridlock.

“Lagos is so unreal mahn. Been stuck in traffic since 8 pm yesterday and I’m just still at Berger,” one X user wrote.

The user blamed the prolonged congestion partly on motorists driving against traffic, saying their actions had reduced the available space for vehicles heading towards Lagos to just one lane.

Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, governorship candidate in Abia State, Kelechi Anosike, has vowed to increase the minimum wage in the state to N90,000 if elected, saying he will introduce a welfarist system that would enable families unable to pay school fees to do so.

content:
By Dickson Omobola

Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, governorship candidate in Abia State, Kelechi Anosike, has vowed to increase the minimum wage in the state to N90,000 if elected, saying he will introduce a welfarist system that would enable families unable to pay school fees to do so.

Anosike also lamented the taxation burden in Abia, saying he would review the tax collection system and charge the rich to service the poor.

He made the promises on The Morning Show, an Arise TV programme, where he said the 15,000 workers sacked before their time would be recalled.

His words: “Let me first tell Abians the political ideology with which we have come and what we intend to do for the state. I am a welfarist, and we have developed a welfarist philosophy and manifesto. For us, the whole essence of government is to serve the people. Without the people, there is no government. At the centre of governance is the people. That’s why we say the people of Abia first. I believe in the good of all mankind, and that’s what we are bringing on board.

“We developed about eight welfarist political philosophies. One of them now is workers’ welfare. As a welfarist, we play by the rules. If the rules say if you get to 60 years, you retire, or if you get to 35 years of age, you retire. If you don’t reach those milestones, we will not retire you. That’s why I told Abians that those 15,000 workers sacked before their time, we will recall them. Because behind every sacked worker is a family struggling to feed.

“We say we will pay a minimum of N90,000. The national benchmark is N70,000; we will do N90,000 minimum wage. With that said, we’ll restore the dignity of the civil service. A situation where directors are using tricycles to go to work, we’ll stop it. We will get it back to what it used to be. You get official cars for directors and for magistrates.

“Within 100 days in office, about three months, we’ll clear all allowances, all pensions, all gratuities. If the rule says that if you are promoted from level 12 to 13, you get your promotion allowance, once we promote you, that allowance should follow you.

“If the rule says that if you apply for annual leave, you get your leave allowance, the moment you are proceeding on annual leave, the leave allowance should follow you. So, we believe that every worker is entitled to his wages. We believe in the motivation of the entire workforce.

“We believe in education and skills. Skills that create opportunities. I said there will be a degree and a skill. Never again will anyone graduate without a skill. There should be a skill and an entrepreneurship grant for those students who have learned skills and want to start a business. The government will give them grants to start a business.

“We will set up a traders’ microfinance bank, headquartered in Aba. There’s a programme we call Operation Feed Abia. Operation Feed Abia. It’s a back-to-farm state policy. If you are eating one meal a day, you will eat three square meals a day.

“There is really excessive taxation going on in Abia. I will not tax a truck pusher. The woman selling akara is being taxed about N500 to N1,000 per day. In seven days, it is N7,000. When you multiply that by 30 days and 12 months, she is being paid close to N300,000 for selling akara. We will review the tax burden, collect from the rich to service the poor.”

title: Saudi says Houthis target Mecca, warns of ‘red line’
description:
The Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen’s Houthis accused them on Wednesday of targeting Islam’s holy city Mecca, sparking outrage across the Muslim world.



The Houthis swiftly rejected as a “lie” Riyadh’s statement that it had shot down a drone heading towards Mecca,
content:
The Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen’s Houthis accused them on Wednesday of targeting Islam’s holy city Mecca, sparking outrage across the Muslim world.

The Houthis swiftly rejected as a “lie” Riyadh’s statement that it had shot down a drone heading towards Mecca, which attracts millions of pilgrims each year.

Fresh fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has dragged in the kingdom, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on its ships in the Red Sea.

Last week, the Houthis seized control of the entirety of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital artery for Saudi oil exports as the wider Middle East war chokes off the Strait of Hormuz shipping route.

“The claims about targeting Mecca are a worn-out lie that has been used before and no longer fools anyone,” Hazem al-Assad from the Houthi politburo wrote on X.

“I saw a few people panicking, running to the window to see what happened,” a Mecca resident who asked for anonymity told AFP.

“I think the alarm system creates panic… Life is normal in Mecca, and there have been previous incidents in Mecca so this isn’t the first one.”

Saudi Arabia accused the Houthis of launching attacks towards Mecca in an earlier conflict.

The Saudi coalition has vowed retaliation, saying that “the security of the Two Holy Mosques and the pilgrims is a red line.”

“The coalition will not hesitate to take the necessary and deterrent measures against the Terrorist Houthi Militia.”

Saudi Arabia had issued brief alerts on Tuesday over possible attacks in Mecca and across parts of the south.

“I won’t hide that we were scared,” a second Mecca resident, also speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP, “or you can say surprised”.

“Aren’t they Muslims? They’re targeting the holiest city. What’s inside to target?”

Mecca hosts a large number of security forces, responsible for crowd control and securing the holy sites, particularly during the annual hajj gathering.

During this year’s pilgrimage, the Saudi defence ministry released a video showing advanced air defence batteries positioned on the outskirts of Mecca.

The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation — a bloc of 57 Muslim countries — condemned the “heinous attacks… against the city of Mecca and the Madinah region”.

Fighting flared in July when the Houthis, who have for years controlled swathes of northern Yemen, launched a large-scale offensive against government forces.

The conflict in the Arabian Peninsula’s poorest country has forced 82,000 people to flee their homes since the start of September, according to the United Nations.

Yemen’s permanent representative at the UN, Abdullah al-Saadi, said the government was fighting to restore “national institutions across every inch” of the country, and called on the international community to take action against the Houthis.

– ‘Catastrophic for entire world’ –

Saadi’s plea came as Saudi Arabia and Egypt called for free navigation in the Red Sea.

De facto Saudi leader Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Tuesday for “ensuring the freedom and security of maritime navigation” through Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, which links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.

The revival of Yemen’s civil war, dormant since 2022, has left Riyadh scrambling to respond.

US media reported last week that the Saudi crown prince made a personal request to President Donald Trump for US intervention, but was turned down.

The Houthis have insisted there is no threat to navigation in Bab al-Mandab except for Saudi vessels, but any attacks in the waterway are likely to make it less attractive to shippers.

Disruption in the strait could cause Egypt to feel the pinch too, as the Red Sea serves as the gateway to the Suez Canal, upon which Cairo relies for crucial foreign revenue.

Canal revenues are currently around half of what they were before the Houthis first started attacking Red Sea shipping in 2023, a campaign they said was in solidarity with Palestinians during Israel’s war against Hamas in Gaza.

On Tuesday, Qatar warned of dire consequences if Bab al-Mandab was closed, saying it would be “catastrophic for the entire world”.

The Houthis have also targeted oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, the world’s leading crude exporter, helping push global prices above the $100-a-barrel threshold.

Riyadh’s retaliatory strikes have failed to reverse the recent gains made by the Houthis, which claimed on Wednesday they had shot down a Saudi fighter jet.

A US military task force is working to enhance intelligence-sharing and planning assistance for Saudi forces, a US official told AFP on Tuesday.

title: Ekiti tribunal considers relocation after alleged assault on counsel

By Rotimi Ojomoyela, Ado-Ekiti



The Ekiti State Governorship Election Petition Tribunal has adjourned further hearing of the petition challenging the outcome of the 2026 governorship election following an application by the petitioners seeking the relocation of the proceedings over an alleged assa
content:
By Rotimi Ojomoyela, Ado-Ekiti

The Ekiti State Governorship Election Petition Tribunal has adjourned further hearing of the petition challenging the outcome of the 2026 governorship election following an application by the petitioners seeking the relocation of the proceedings over an alleged assault on counsel to the Social Democratic Party (SDP).

The three-member tribunal, chaired by Justice Abubakar Kutigi, adjourned the matter until September 23, 2026, to allow the President of the Court of Appeal to determine the petitioners’ request for the transfer of the case to another venue they consider safe.

Speaking with journalists after Wednesday’s proceedings, counsel to the All Progressives Congress (APC) and Governor Biodun Oyebanji, Adetunji Osho, SAN, said counsel to the petitioners, Ebenezer Akinbule, appeared before the tribunal on Tuesday but was unable to produce witnesses.

According to Osho, Akinbule attributed his inability to present the witnesses to a crisis allegedly affecting the proceedings and subsequently sought an adjournment.

He said the respondents saw Akinbule and some of his witnesses within the tribunal premises on Tuesday.

Osho said the respondents were surprised when they were served with a letter on Wednesday seeking another adjournment on the grounds that Akinbule had allegedly been assaulted and that some of the witnesses were being prevented from appearing before the tribunal.

He further disclosed that the petitioners had written to the President of the Court of Appeal, requesting that the petition be transferred from Ekiti State to another location they considered safe.

Osho said the tribunal, in view of the application before the President of the Court of Appeal, adjourned the matter until September 23 for the application for transfer to be considered.

He said the respondents had no option but to concede to the adjournment pending the determination of the venue application.

Osho said: “The hearing of the petition commenced on the 8th of September 2026 and, as is usual, the hearing was to go on day-to-day. It was then adjourned today for continuation of hearing.

“Yesterday, the petitioner’s counsel, one Ebenezer Akinbule, was in court, and he admitted that the crisis that is rocking the area prevented him from bringing his witnesses and applied that the matter be adjourned today.

“We saw him and his witnesses yesterday within the court premises and until he drove off.

“Today, we were surprised to be served with a letter asking for an adjournment on the ground that he was assaulted and that his witnesses were being prevented from coming to the tribunal.

“We were also informed that he had written to the President of the Court of Appeal for a change of venue and that the petition be transferred from Ekiti to another venue which they consider safe for them.

“The tribunal, in its wisdom, adjourned the hearing of the petition till Wednesday, 23rd of September, for the President of the Court of Appeal to take a decision on the petitioner’s application for transfer of the petition.

“So, we are constrained to concede to the adjournment, and then we will await the President of the Court of Appeal’s decision on the petitioner’s application for transfer of the petition out of Ado-Ekiti.”

title: 20 countries moving to ban social media for children
description:

More than 20 countries around the world have now taken steps to block or restrict childre
content:
The European Union is to unveil proposals Wednesday aimed at curbing addictive features of social media for minors, as a growing number of countries look to restrict children’s access to the platforms.

More than 20 countries around the world have now taken steps to block or restrict children going online on social media, according to an AFP tally.

Seven have measures already in place or set to be implemented, with their policies targeting children under the age of 15 or 16.

Australia was the first country to introduce a blanket ban on social media for under-16s, at the end of 2025.

The US state of California has also recently moved to tighten restrictions on minors’ access to social media.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is due to present her proposals to the European Parliament on Wednesday, after months of considering ways to protect minors from features designed to keep users hooked.

– Restrictions in place –

Social media has been banned for under-16s in Australia since December 2025.

However, the ban so far appears to have been widely circumvented by teenagers, according to data released in August.

Brazil began implementing measures in March requiring platforms to link the accounts of users aged under 16 to those of their parents, while also requiring platforms to verify users’ ages.

In China, where the internet is tightly regulated by the state, minors’ access to social media has been restricted progressively since 2019.

Initial measures imposed time limits and curfews on online gaming, before similar restrictions were extended in 2023 to social media and streaming platforms.

Indonesia has banned social media for under-16s since March.

Malaysia has taken a similar approach, with legislation coming into force in June excluding under-16s from major platforms.

Turkey is set to join the list after passing legislation to bar under-15s from social media in April.

The law is expected to take effect in late 2026.

The United Arab Emirates announced a ban on social media for under-15s last month, with implementation set for around in a year’s time.

The governor of the US state of California, Gavin Newsom, signed around a dozen laws on September 10 aimed at protecting children online, including one banning platforms from offering addictive features to under-16s. The law will take effect in early 2027.

– Restrictions announced –

Across the 27-nation EU, the Greek government announced in early April that it intends to ban social media access for under-15s from January 2027.

Austria and Slovenia are also preparing legislation to prohibit access for under-14s and under-15s, respectively.

In Germany, where Chancellor Friedrich Merz supports restricting or even banning social media for children, an expert commission has proposed two options: gradual restrictions by age, or platform-specific restrictions.

A similar debate is under way in Sweden, where a government commission has proposed banning social media for under-15s by early 2028.

In Denmark, the government announced in October 2025 that it would propose banning “several social media platforms” for under-15s.

The Irish government has warned that it is considering legislating in the absence of an EU decision.

Outside the EU, the Norwegian government will present a bill by the end of the year to ban access for those under 16.

Britain is looking to ban social media for under-16s by early 2027 under a measure planned by its former prime minister, Keir Starmer.

A curfew would also be implemented for children aged 16 and 17 as part of the plan.

Canada unveiled a bill on June 10 that would also set the minimum age at 16.

New Zealand followed Australia’s lead in August with a bill that would ban social media platforms from offering their services to under-16s.

– Bills in parliament –

In Portugal, lawmakers from the ruling right-wing party introduced a bill in February that would set the age of “digital majority” at 16 for independent access to social media platforms, online services, games and apps.

In Spain, a bill unveiled in March 2025 and now under consideration would raise the minimum age for opening a social media account to 16.

Italy is also considering legislation that would ban social media for under-15s.

In France, parliament approved legislation this summer to ban social media for under-15s, but the Constitutional Council, the country’s highest constitutional authority, struck it down on freedom-of-expression grounds.

President Emmanuel Macron has pledged to introduce a new “legally robust” law by spring 2027.

AFP

content:
Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has given criminals operating in the state’s forest reserves 14 days to vacate the forests.

The Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Forestry, Mr Bidemi Obayangban, made this known in an interview with newsmen on Wednesday in Akure.

According to Obayangban, the governor’s directive is particularly targeted at kidnappers and other criminals using the forests as hideouts.

He said it was part of measures to improve security and create a safe environment for legitimate economic activities.

Obayangban said security remained a prerequisite for the state government’s plans to develop the forestry sector and attract investors.

“A vision without maximum security to ensure the safety of investors, farmers, timber contractors and those conducting legitimate business across Ondo State’s forest reserves is effectively meaningless,” he said.

He said the administration had concluded plans to tackle kidnapping and other criminal activities in the state’s forests.

According to him, security agencies and hunters across the state were collaborating with the government in the effort to restore security to the forest reserves.

“Consequently, the primary focus of the Aiyedatiwa administration is to flush out criminal elements from our forests. We are taking the battle directly to them.

“The government is fully committed to this objective and has finalised comprehensive plans to eliminate kidnapping and other illegal activities within our borders,” he said.

Obayangban said the governor preferred a discreet and action-oriented approach to security matters, but stressed that the government was determined to reclaim the forests from criminal elements.

“I am using this opportunity to announce that the state government is giving these individuals 14 days to vacate Ondo State forests.

“Failure to comply will result in them meeting their Waterloo,” he said.

Obayangban said restoring security to the forests was also critical to the government’s broader plan to revitalise the forestry sector and promote legitimate economic activities.

He said the administration recognised that sustainable economic growth could not be achieved in an environment where farmers, investors and other legitimate operators were exposed to insecurity.

ABUJA—A former President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Chief Ebele Nwokoye, has been conferred with the Blue Silk rank, an honour introduced as an alternative to the Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) title for non-litigation lawyers in Nigeria.

content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA—A former President of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Chief Ebele Nwokoye, has been conferred with the Blue Silk rank, an honour introduced as an alternative to the Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) title for non-litigation lawyers in Nigeria.

The introduction of the title had been the subject of a legal battle between the NBA and promoters of the rank, the Association of Legislative Drafting and Advocacy Practitioners (ALDRAP).

Both the NBA and the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, had opposed the introduction of the “Blue Silks,” describing the title as illegal.

Likewise, the Legal Practitioners’ Privileges Committee (LPPC) disowned the Blue Silk title, insisting that the rank of SAN remained the highest mark of professional distinction for legal practitioners in the country.

Maintaining that the “Blue Silk” rank has no statutory backing, the LPPC warned that its use could amount to a violation of the provisions of the Rules of Professional Conduct for Legal Practitioners 2023.

However, the award of the rank to a former President of the NBA appears to be a major twist in the controversy.

Nwokoye, who served as NBA President from 1985 to 1987, was conferred with the Blue Silk rank on Tuesday at an event in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State.

He was also conferred with the title of National Patron of the Body of Senior Counsel of Nigeria (BOSCON).

BOSCON is the body responsible for the assessment and conferment of candidates who apply for the Blue Silk rank.

Unlike the rank of SAN, whose major criterion is the submission of evidence of courtroom litigation by candidates, the criteria for the Blue Silk rank require candidates to submit not less than 35 verifiable non-litigation transactions, as well as hold a Bachelor of Laws (LLB) degree for not less than ten years.

Reacting to the development in a statement, the Executive Secretary of ALDRAP, Dr Tonye Clinton Jaja, noted that September 15, 2026, will be remembered in the history of the Nigerian legal profession as the date the Blue Silk rank of Senior Counsel of Nigeria (SCN) secured a double victory.

“The conferment of the Blue Silks-SCN upon the former President of the NBA, Chief Nwokoye, is a significant victory, considering that the immediate past leadership of the NBA launched an unsuccessful attack against the Blue Silks-SCN at its inception in 2025.

“Instead of filing a lawsuit in a court of law, the Mazi Afam Osigwe-led regime of the NBA unsuccessfully tried to use illegal methods to stop the maiden investiture ceremony, which was held at the Federal Secretariat Complex, Abuja, Federal Capital Territory (FCT), on 15th December 2025.

“Without any court order, the Mazi Afam Osigwe-led NBA regime mobilised police officers and other officials of the National Assembly (including the Clerk to the National Assembly, Mr Kamoru Ogunlana, Esq.) to deny entry into the hall at the Senate building of the National Assembly, where the investiture ceremony was originally scheduled to hold.

“All the aforementioned illegal methods and the resort to self-help, instead of recourse to a court of law, by the Mazi Afam Osigwe-led regime of the NBA are what the Supreme Court of Nigeria condemned in its landmark judgment in Governor of Lagos State v. Ojukwu (1986) 1 Nigerian Weekly Law Reports (NWLR) (Pt. 18) 621.

“It must be noted that all these illegal methods were deployed by the Mazi Afam Osigwe-led regime of the NBA even after they were officially informed that the promoters of the Blue Silks-SCN had filed a lawsuit against the Incorporated Trustees of the NBA at the Federal High Court, Abuja, seeking an order of injunction against the NBA’s interference with the Blue Silks-SCN.

“Ironically, the same Mazi Afam Osigwe-led regime of the NBA immediately raised the alarm and relied on the defence that the Incorporated Trustees of the NBA is an independent legal entity that cannot allow external interference from the Hon. Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice. This was the same defence raised by Mazi Afam Osigwe during the July 2026 election of the National Officers of the NBA,” he stated.

Continuing, Jaja noted that the period within which the NBA could appeal the Abuja Federal High Court judgment affirming the conferment of the Blue Silks has passed.

“The second part of the victory is that the time prescribed for the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) to file its appeal has elapsed, and the NBA has failed to file any appeal against the said judgment, which validates the Blue Silks-SCN.

“The judgment was delivered on 27th January 2026 by Hon. Justice Mohammed Umar Garba of the Federal High Court, Abuja, Suit Number FHC/ABJ/CS/1238/2025,” he added.

According to him, the judgment prohibited the NBA, and by extension the LPPC, from attempting to regulate the Blue Silk rank and any other matters not expressly mentioned in the Legal Practitioners Act, 1962.

“The NBA, who were parties in the said lawsuit, failed to appeal that judgment. Therefore, it remains the binding judgment,” Jaja said, noting that instead of appealing, the NBA is relying on another judgment by a different judge of the same Federal High Court, Abuja, which has itself been appealed.

He insisted that the Blue Silk title, introduced as an alternative to the rank of SAN, is a legally recognised route to legal excellence for non-litigation lawyers in the country.

title: Rivers, Kwara, Gombe, Cross River: APC states threatened by Wike’s Rainbow Coalition ahead of 2027
description:
Powerful blocs within the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, are increasingly concerned about the spread of the National Rainbow Coalition, backed by Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, across states controlled by the ruling party.







The coalition, which Wike insist
content:
Powerful blocs within the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, are increasingly concerned about the spread of the National Rainbow Coalition, backed by Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Nyesom Wike, across states controlled by the ruling party.

The coalition, which Wike insists is primarily aimed at securing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, has nevertheless thrown up alliances involving opposition parties and politicians opposed to APC candidates at state and National Assembly levels.

The development has raised particular concerns in Rivers, Kwara, Gombe and Cross River, where coalition-backed candidates and political realignments are challenging existing APC structures.

APC governors and their allies are worried that the arrangement could create confusion among voters and weaken the party’s candidates in elections taking place alongside the presidential poll.

Wike, however, has maintained that his political objective is to support Tinubu while working with politicians across party lines.

Speaking during a media chat in Port Harcourt, Wike specifically accused Imo State Governor and Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum, Senator Hope Uzodimma, and Kwara State Governor and Chairman of the Nigeria Governors Forum, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, of campaigning against him.

“Take, for example, Kwara; he has been the one championing this campaign against me. Yes, I have confronted him too. I don’t talk about what I cannot defend,” Wike said.

He accused AbdulRazaq of alleging that he was sponsoring candidates against the governor’s preferred choices in Kwara while arguing that he had provided a political platform for aggrieved APC members who could otherwise have joined groups opposed to Tinubu.

The concerns among APC leaders are particularly pronounced in states where politicians who have fallen out with the ruling party are now working with the Rainbow Coalition.

Rivers

Rivers presents one of the most complicated fronts for the APC, with the coalition drawing members from the PDP, APC, Labour Party and other political groups.

The coalition emerged in January 2026 during the political crisis involving Wike and Governor Siminalayi Fubara. Its political significance increased after Fubara joined the APC.

The coalition has since generated uncertainty over the governorship race, particularly after it backed former PDP Minority Leader in the House of Representatives, Kingsley Chinda, for governor.

Chinda, who had been a PDP lawmaker, appeared before the APC screening committee after his defection, although the circumstances surrounding his move remain the subject of litigation.

The choice of Chinda has also reportedly generated disquiet among some coalition members from the riverine areas, who argue that a candidate from the area should have been preferred.

The coalition subsequently picked Major Jack, the current Majority Leader of the Rivers State House of Assembly, as Chinda’s running mate.

The arrangement has created a situation in which Rivers voters could face different candidates representing parties that are simultaneously claiming membership of the same coalition.

Kwara

Kwara has emerged as another major battleground between the APC structure and politicians aligned with Wike’s coalition.

The conflict intensified after a group of aggrieved APC members joined forces with former Senate President Bukola Saraki and the Wike-backed PDP structure in the state.

Senator Saliu Mustapha, who contested the APC governorship primary and later faced a battle over his return to the Senate, subsequently resigned from the APC and joined the PDP.

He was given the PDP ticket for Kwara Central, setting up a contest with Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq.

Another APC chieftain, Kolo Jiya, also left the party and joined the PDP, while two members of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Olushola Odetundun and Saba Yisa Gideon, defected to the PDP.

The aggrieved APC members subsequently came together under the Otoge Progressives, T.O.P., and formally launched the Kwara chapter of the National Rainbow Coalition on August 26, 2026.

The coalition says its arrangement allows politicians to support Tinubu for president while retaining the freedom to support different parties in other elections.

Gombe

In Gombe, former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Pantami, has moved to the PDP with the backing of the Rainbow Coalition.

The development has created another unusual political alignment, with the coalition seeking to support Tinubu at the presidential level while simultaneously working against APC structures at the state level.

The situation illustrates the central dilemma confronting APC leaders: politicians can support the president while campaigning against candidates of the party on whose platform he is seeking re-election.

Cross River

Cross River is another state where the coalition is challenging APC structures.

The PDP has an active governorship candidate, Arthur Jarvis, while the party also has candidates contesting senatorial, House of Representatives and House of Assembly seats.

About 500 APC members recently defected to the PDP in the state, according to the report.

Why APC governors are worried

The central concern among APC figures is that the Rainbow Coalition’s multi-party structure could undermine President Tinubu’s re-election.

Beyond this, the governors argued that ahead of the 2027 elections, Wike’s arraignment could weaken the APC and that they won’t support or endorse candidates who are not members of the party in the 2027 elections.

Speaking with journalists at the end of APC Governors Forum meeting on Monday night in Abuja, Imo state governor and secretary of the Tinubu Campaign Council, Hope Uzodimma, said, “The APC Governors Forum unanimously resolved that its members will not participate in, support or endorse any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining the re-election of Mr President, weakening the APC or adversely affecting any candidate of the party at all levels.

“In other words, the forum has no intention to support any candidate at any level that is not an APC candidate because our candidates who are contesting the election are being sponsored by our party.”

He added that the APC’s campaign activities at all levels would focus exclusively on the party’s candidates and align with Mr Tinubu’s agenda.

“The governors’ campaign commitment is exclusively to all APC candidates. All levels of the party campaign architecture will align with the expectations of Mr President and the strategic objectives of the party.”

Wike has remained defiant

Wike, however, maintained that the Rainbow Coalition was created to mobilise support for President Tinubu’s re-election and had nothing to do with the APC or its candidates in other elections.

In a statement by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, the FCT minister insisted his support for 2027 was specifically for Tinubu and did not amount to a commitment that the PDP would not field candidates in other elections.

“What I said and stand for is that I will mobilise support for the re-election of the President. I never promised anyone that PDP will not field candidates to contest governorship, National Assembly and States House of Assembly elections,” Wike said.

He also dismissed the suggestion that the Rainbow Coalition was an arrangement with the APC, describing it as a platform for members of different political parties supporting Tinubu’s re-election.

“Most importantly, Rainbow Coalition has nothing to do with the APC. Rather, it is our own way of mobilising support across political parties for Mr President, who has done well to deserve a second term,” he added.

Wike further challenged Uzodimma over APC’s performance in the 2023 elections in Imo and other South-East states, questioning how the party won legislative seats despite recording a much lower share of the presidential vote.

“Was it Rainbow Coalition that also made APC to win National Assembly elections in Ebonyi, Abia and Enugu states where the president did not have ten per cent of the votes?” he asked.

title: Four Killed, One Injured In Fatal Crash On Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
description: Four people have been killed and one other injured in a road crash along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway in Ogun State.The Ogun State Command of the Federal Road Safety Corps confirmed the crash, saying eight people were involved in the incident.The command’s spokesperson, Afolabi Odunsin, said pr
content:
Four people have been killed and one other injured in a road crash along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway in Ogun State.

The Ogun State Command of the Federal Road Safety Corps confirmed the crash, saying eight people were involved in the incident.

The command’s spokesperson, Afolabi Odunsin, said preliminary investigations showed that the crash was caused by speeding and wrongful overtaking.

He said the driver of a Mitsubishi Cabstar, which was travelling at high speed, rammed into a moving truck while attempting to overtake.

“Fatigue was also identified as a contributing factor, as the driver was reportedly fatigued during the journey,” Odunsin said.

According to the FRSC, four male adults died in the crash, while another male adult sustained injuries. Three other people escaped unhurt.

Two vehicles were involved in the crash, a blue Mitsubishi Cabstar with registration number FGE 753 XA and an ash-coloured HOWO truck with registration number T-695 KT.

The FRSC spokesperson said the injured victim was rescued and taken to Victory Hospital, Ogere, for medical attention.

The bodies of the deceased were deposited at the FOS Mortuary, Ipara.

Odunsin added that the crashed vehicles had been handed over to the Police Motor Traffic Division, Isara Division, for further investigation and necessary action.

The Sector Commander, Corps Commander Oludare Ogunjobi, urged motorists to avoid speeding, fatigue and unsafe overtaking, particularly during early-morning journeys.

He also advised drivers embarking on long-distance trips to get adequate rest before travelling and to overtake only when it is safe and permissible.

The fatal crash occurred amid a difficult period for motorists using the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, with the corridor already experiencing severe congestion linked to ongoing repairs on the Kara Bridge.

The Federal Government commenced a two-week rehabilitation of the bridge on September 8, involving the replacement of damaged expansion joints. The repair work has reduced available road space and triggered prolonged delays for motorists travelling between Lagos and Ogun State.

The traffic situation worsened significantly on Tuesday after multiple crashes around the Kara Bridge, including an incident involving a 40-foot container-laden truck.

The incidents compounded the existing restrictions from the bridge repairs and left motorists trapped for more than 14 hours in some sections.

According to reports, the resulting gridlock stretched beyond Long Bridge towards Magboro and into Lagos, while some motorists were forced to spend several hours on the road or seek alternative means of reaching their destinations.

By Wednesday morning, traffic was still moving slowly around the Kara Bridge and OPIC turning, with the backlog extending beyond Long Bridge, according to traffic updates.

The prolonged congestion has also left commuters complaining about long hours on the road, increased transport fares and lost working hours, with some reporting that they had trekked considerable distances after becoming stranded.

The situation has further heightened concerns about road safety along the busy corridor, where reduced road capacity due to the ongoing repairs means that crashes or broken-down vehicles can quickly trigger extensive gridlock.

Authorities have continued to deploy traffic management personnel to the corridor while efforts are ongoing to maintain movement and reduce the impact of the bridge rehabilitation.

The Federal Government has said the Kara Bridge repairs are expected to continue until September 22.

title: Olu Jacobs was a national icon — Omokri
description:

Omokri, in a statement following the
content:
Nigeria’s Ambassador-designate to Mexico, Reno Omokri, has described the late veteran actor, Oludotun Baiyewu Jacobs, popularly known as Olu Jacobs, as a national icon whose pioneering career on the international stage inspired generations of Nigerian actors.

Omokri, in a statement following the announcement of Jacobs’ death at the age of 84, said the late actor played a significant role in laying the foundation for the contemporary African film industry.

He said Jacobs broke international barriers long before Nollywood became a global phenomenon and brought pride to Nigerians through his performances in British television productions and international films.

“Oludotun Baiyewu Jacobs, better known as Olu Jacobs, was a National Icon and a source of pride for Nigeria, whose pioneering role as an international thespian inspired many of our countrymen and women and drew many of today’s stars into television and movie acting,” Omokri said.

Recalling his childhood memories, the ambassador-designate said Nigerians watched Jacobs feature in British television shows and international movies, noting that the actor received professional training at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art (RADA) in London.

“As children, we watched in awe as one of us starred in multiple British sitcoms and several global blockbuster movies,” he said, citing Jacobs’ appearance in the British television series, The Professionals.

Omokri also described Jacobs as one of the foundational figures of Nigeria’s modern film industry, placing him alongside his mentor, the late Chief Hubert Ogunde.

“Along with his mentor, the late great Chief Hubert Ogunde, he was the real Grand Old Man of Nollywood, having become a global star as far back as the seventies and early eighties,” he said.

He cited Jacobs’ appearances in international productions including The Dogs of War, in which he starred alongside Hollywood actor Christopher Walken, and Roman Polanski’s Pirates.

Omokri further said Jacobs’ humility had contributed to some people making claims to the title of Nollywood pioneer, but maintained that the actor’s body of work spoke for itself.

“Because of the modesty of Ogunde and Jacobs, and especially Mr Jacobs, who starred in hundreds of Nollywood movies, less deserving individuals have made pretences to their title of Nollywood Pioneers, but history makes their claims hollow,” he said.

Mourning the veteran actor, Omokri offered his condolences to Jacobs’ family, particularly his wife, veteran actress Joke Silva, and their children.

“We pray that God Almighty grant the family he left behind succour, especially Auntie Joke Silva, his wife and fellow actor, and their children,” he said.

Omokri also expressed gratitude that Jacobs was honoured by the Nigerian government during his lifetime with the Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR) national honour.

content:
Dozens of people have been arrested in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) following protests against a proposed constitutional amendment that could allow President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a third term.

The protests broke out on Tuesday in Kinshasa, the capital, and several other major cities, with police using force to disperse demonstrators.

According to Reuters, police fired tear gas and warning shots in Kinshasa to disperse hundreds of protesters who participated in the demonstrations.

Videos shared on social media showed protesters waving flags belonging to various political parties during demonstrations organised by Coalition Article 64 (C64), a broad opposition alliance opposed to the proposed constitutional amendments.

Tshisekedi, who has been president since 2019, is due to complete his second five-year term in 2028. Under the current constitution, he would be ineligible to seek another term.

However, the 63-year-old president said last month that he would be willing to serve a third term in the conflict-plagued country “if the people wish it.”

In June, months before Tshisekedi made the remarks, the DRC Senate passed a bill providing for the holding of referendums in the country.

The protests reportedly escalated after supporters and opponents of Tshisekedi clashed during demonstrations over the proposed constitutional changes, prompting police to intervene.

Martin Fayulu, a former presidential candidate and one of the leaders of C64, said the opposition was considering filing an international complaint against Tshisekedi over the alleged violence against opposition activists.

title: Lagos-Ibadan Expressway: When Repairs Leave Commuters Caught In A Traffic Storm
description: For most workers, an eight-hour workday is already demanding. But for commuters along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, hours are now being spent not at their desks but trapped in traffic.The busy corridor has endured repeated bouts of severe congestion in 2026, with repair works, overturned trucks, fall
content:
For most workers, an eight-hour workday is already demanding. But for commuters along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, hours are now being spent not at their desks but trapped in traffic.

The busy corridor has endured repeated bouts of severe congestion in 2026, with repair works, overturned trucks, fallen containers, and road crashes repeatedly disrupting movement between Lagos and Ogun State.

The latest disruption came on Tuesday, when a container-laden trailer fell on Kara Bridge, forcing the total closure of the Lagos-bound section and worsening congestion already caused by ongoing rehabilitation works. The resulting gridlock stretched beyond Berger, while motorists heading in the opposite direction were forced to share the available section of the expressway.

For commuters caught in the resulting standstill, the difference between a routine journey and an ordeal can be several hours.

And The Menace

For entrepreneur Nsikak Akpan, what should have been a 15-minute journey home turned into a seven-hour ordeal.

“I spent seven hours at Ojodu Berger area, just trying to connect the express. I had to find a hotel to sleep. That was 15 minutes away from home on a normal day.”

Akpan’s experience captures the scale of disruption that can occur when traffic on the corridor loses its normal rhythm, with some arriving home late from work and their businesses into the night, missing appointments, and, in some cases, abandoning their journeys altogether.

Nine-to-five worker Samuel Markson said he eventually decided to return home rather than remain trapped in traffic.

“I’m officially going back home; I cannot come and kill myself. Traffic has turned my bus stop into a permanent landmark. Standstill everywhere, and not a single yellow bus in sight.” Markson said

The prolonged gridlock has also become a question of health and well-being for commuters who spend hours sitting in stationary vehicles or waiting at increasingly crowded bus stops.

“At this point, work can continue without me,” said an exhausted Markson. “Even commuters at the bus stop are going back home, and why should I not join them? My health is more important.”

Beyond the frustration and anger of long hours on the road, the gridlock has also been worsened by the impatience of drivers and the actions of some motorists who drive against traffic, further disrupting movement for other road users.

The gridlock on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway has also spilled into surrounding roads, with a backlog of traffic extending to the 7Up, Ogudu and Iyana-Oworo axis as motorists search for alternative ways through the wider network.

Commuters are stranded at bus stops, while for some, trekking has become the only option to reach their destinations, almost like a new sport.

“I trekked to work this morning. Never done it in my life. And the traffic is at a standstill,” Favor said.

Repairs Meet A Fragile Corridor

The project, directed by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, involves the replacement of deteriorating expansion joints and commenced on September 8, 2026. It is scheduled to run until September 22.

The repairs were announced in advance, with authorities explaining that one half of the affected section would be closed at a time while traffic was managed on the remaining half. The work is intended to improve the structural condition and long-term safety of the bridge.

But the beginning of the exercise immediately demonstrated the difficulty of repairing a critical transport artery that carries large volumes of traffic, with at least 200,000 commuters every day.

On September 9, motorists were stranded for several hours, with congestion stretching from Kara Bridge towards 7Up Junction and beyond. Traffic from Ikeja and Agege attempting to access the Otedola underpass was also caught in the congestion.

The repair work itself, therefore, became only one part of the problem. With available road space reduced, any additional disruption has the potential to magnify delays across a much wider area.

And that is precisely what happened when the container-laden trailer fell on Wednesday, September 15.

When Trucks Bring Traffic To A Halt

The fallen container on Kara Bridge transformed an already difficult traffic situation into a more severe standstill.

The incident forced the complete closure of the Lagos-bound section of the bridge, while motorists travelling in the opposite direction had to share one side of the expressway. Authorities subsequently began removing barriers from another section of the bridge to create an alternative passage. Officials of the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority and traffic officials from Ogun State were deployed to manage the situation.

The incident was not an isolated example of how articulated vehicles and accidents can paralyse the corridor.

In July 2026, a multiple-vehicle crash on Kara Bridge left one person dead and others injured, while hundreds of motorists were stranded. The crash involved five articulated trucks and a Toyota Sienna on the outbound carriageway towards Ibadan, with traffic backing up to Otedola Bridge and affecting the Isheri-Olowora axis and Ogunusi Road.

In March, a heavy-duty truck carrying two 20-foot containers overturned on Otedola Bridge after reportedly developing a mechanical fault. The resulting congestion extended beyond Kara Bridge and caused significant delays for commuters and motorists.

Route Where Minutes Multiply

The recurring pattern illustrates the particular vulnerability of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. It is not simply a road connecting two major cities; it is a major route through which commuters, commercial vehicles, articulated trucks and travellers move between Lagos and other parts of the country.

When an accident occurs, the consequences can quickly extend beyond the immediate crash scene.

A January crash on Otedola Bridge, for example, obstructed nearly 80 per cent of the carriageway, according to LASTMA, prompting extensive traffic control and diversions. Motorists travelling from the Mowe, Kara Bridge and Redemption Camp axis were redirected through alternative routes towards Ojota and Gbagada.

Another crash on Kara Bridge in January involved a truck, a Toyota Corolla, an RAV4 SUV and two interstate buses. The incident caused severe congestion and left motorists stranded for hours before recovery operations helped restore movement.

The problem is consequently cumulative. Repair works reduce available road space. A fallen truck or container can block more of what remains. An accident can then trigger a backlog that spreads into adjoining roads, while motorists seeking alternatives add pressure to already busy routes.

For those caught inside the resulting chain, a journey that ordinarily takes minutes can consume an entire morning or working day.

The authorities have repeatedly urged motorists to exercise patience and cooperate with traffic managers. During the current Kara Bridge rehabilitation, the Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency said traffic had been anticipated and called on motorists to bear with the situation.

“We anticipated that there would be traffic, and that was why we issued a traffic advisory earlier.

“We can only appeal to motorists to bear with us for the time being because the repair works are necessary to ensure smooth movement and the safety of road users along the corridor,” it said.

“Anyone who does not have an important business along the axis should stay away, and those who cannot avoid using that route should cooperate with traffic officials.”

For commuters, however, patience is being tested against the practical demands of work, business, family and travel.

The rehabilitation of Kara Bridge is scheduled to end on September 22. Until then, traffic managers face the difficult task of keeping vehicles moving through a corridor where every additional obstruction can have consequences far beyond the point where it occurs.

For the millions who depend on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, the hope is that the repair work will ultimately deliver the safer and more reliable corridor it is intended to create.

But for those sitting in stationary vehicles today, the question is much more immediate: how many more hours will it take to reach the destination?

The post Lagos-Ibadan Expressway: When Repairs Leave Commuters Caught In A Traffic Storm appeared first on Channels Television.
