content:
Veteran Nigerian actor and elder statesman, Oludotun Baiyewu Jacobs, popularly known as Olu Jacobs, has died at the age of 84.

PUNCH Online reports that his death was announced by his son, Olusoji Jacobs, on Instagram on Wednesday.

Olu Jacobs was one of Nigeria’s most respected actors and a towering figure in the country’s theatre, television and film industries.

For more than five decades, Jacobs built a career that took him from the stage in Britain to international films and, ultimately, to becoming one of the most recognisable faces of Nollywood.

Early life

Born on July 11, 1942, in Kano, Jacobs had his roots in the Egba Alake community of Abeokuta, Ogun State. He grew up in Kano, where he developed an early interest in acting through school drama, debating activities, and church programmes.

His passion for the performing arts was strengthened after he watched a performance by legendary Nigerian theatre practitioner Hubert Ogunde. The experience inspired him to pursue acting professionally.

Training in Britain

Jacobs later travelled to the United Kingdom, where he studied at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London.

His training at RADA gave him a strong foundation in theatre and professional acting. He subsequently worked with several repertoire theatres in Britain and appeared in British television productions.

During the 1970s, he featured in television programmes including The Goodies, Till Death Us Do Part, The Professionals, The Tomorrow People and Barlow at Large.

His international film credits also included The Dogs of War in 1980, Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend in 1985 and Roman Polanski’s Pirates in 1986.

Career spanning generations

After establishing himself in Britain, Jacobs returned to Nigeria and became a major figure in the country’s growing entertainment industry.

His career covered theatre, television and film, with the actor appearing in hundreds of productions over the years.

In Nollywood, Jacobs became particularly known for playing kings, chiefs, traditional rulers, patriarchs and other authoritative characters.

His deep voice, commanding presence and theatrical training made him one of the most recognisable veteran actors on the African continent.

He was widely regarded as part of the generation of actors who helped lay the foundation for the Nigerian film industry as it is known today.

Awards and recognition

Jacobs received several major honours during his career.

In 2007, he won the Africa Movie Academy Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role.

He was also honoured with the Industry Merit Award for outstanding achievement in acting at the 2013 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards and received the MAA Lifetime Achievement Award in 2016.

In 2011, the Federal Government conferred on him the national honour of Member of the Order of the Federal Republic in recognition of his contribution to the Nigerian arts.

Marriage

Jacobs was married to fellow veteran actress Joke Silva. Their relationship developed into both a personal and professional partnership that became one of the most prominent unions in Nigeria’s entertainment industry.

Together, they founded the Lufodo Group, with interests spanning film production, distribution, and performing arts education.

The couple also established the Lufodo Academy of Performing Arts, contributing to the training and development of a new generation of performers.

His later years

Jacobs spent his later years largely away from the public spotlight after his health began to affect his appearances.

Silva had previously disclosed that her husband was dealing with dementia with Lewy bodies, a degenerative condition that affected his health.

The actor’s health also became the subject of repeated false reports of his death. In June 2024, Silva again dismissed reports that he had died, saying he was alive and doing fine. His family had similarly rejected earlier death rumours.

Jacobs subsequently remained largely out of public view, while colleagues and admirers continued to celebrate his contribution to Nigerian theatre and cinema.

A lasting legacy

Olu Jacobs left behind a legacy that extended beyond the characters he played on screen.

His career connected Nigeria’s traditional theatre tradition with modern film and television, while his training and experience abroad added an international dimension to his work.

Through acting, production and arts education, he influenced several generations of Nigerian performers.

Together with contemporaries such as Pete Edochie, he became associated with the generation of veteran actors who helped shape Nollywood and establish its distinctive identity.

For decades, audiences knew him for his portrayal of authority, wisdom and dignity. His performances, awards, mentorship and contribution to the development of the performing arts ensured that his name remained firmly embedded in the history of Nigerian entertainment.

Olu Jacobs died in the early hours of Wednesday, leaving behind his wife, Joke Silva, his family, colleagues and generations of actors and filmmakers influenced by his work.

content:
At 16, Nigerian chess player Sandra Omoruyi is aiming higher after winning the World Rapid Amateur Chess Championship in Abuja in August. In this interview with EBENEZER BAJELA, she reflects on her journey, sacrifices, training and ambitions in chess and medicine

How did you first get introduced to chess, and who were the people who helped shape your early development?

I come from a chess family where my dad, mum and siblings all play chess, so my dad was my first coach. My siblings then taught me how to record moves until I met my present coach, Edward Eguavoe Evbuomwan, Coach Eddy. Some other people also played one or two roles in my growth. I may not be able to mention everyone, but they include Coach Ann, Coach Marian, Coach Ben, Coach Illoba, Coach Nosa and Coach Segun. When I won the MVP at the last Youth Games, I was initially just playing to learn and enjoy the game. After the event, I started thinking, “Maybe I can actually do this at the highest level.” That moment gave me the confidence to take chess more seriously and aim for bigger titles like the World Amateur Championship.

What challenges have you faced since taking up chess, and what do you remember about your first major tournament?

One of the biggest challenges has been not being able to attend tournaments because of distance and finances, and sometimes insecurity in Nigeria, especially as a minor. My first major tournament was the National Chess Championship. At first, I was scared, but after the event, I realised that I could actually do it, even though it was hard.

How demanding is your training routine, particularly when preparing for major competitions?

My training time runs between 10 and 16 hours daily, depending on the day of the week. On mild days, my training starts at 9am or 10am and ends around 10pm or 11pm, with breaks of three to four hours in between for lunch, dinner and school runs. On difficult days, the starting time is the same, but training ends by 2am or 3am the next day. This was basically to play practice games with engines in preparation for the Olympiad. My training schedule and routine are extensive, covering different areas of chess depending on what Coach Eddy plans for that day.

With such a demanding training schedule, how do you balance chess with school and family life?

It’s all about planning and discipline. School and family come first. I use evenings and weekends for chess training. My family is very supportive, and they help me stay focused.

What did it mean to win the World Rapid Amateur Chess Championship in Abuja in August, and how did you prepare for the tournament?

I really didn’t know what I was expecting. I just knew that I had to win because a lot was at stake. My preparation was very focused. For weeks before the tournament, I worked with my coach on Rapid and Blitz-specific training. We did a lot of tactical puzzles because those formats are all about quick accuracy. I also played many Rapid and Blitz games with his students, especially his son, Henry Evbuomwan, to get used to the time pressure. Off the board, I made sure to rest well, stay active and work on my mindset, telling myself to take it one game at a time and not get overwhelmed by the title.

The most difficult moment for me was at the start of the Blitz event. I lost my first three games. Honestly, I was down. I started asking myself, “Is this really happening? Did I travel all this way to lose?” But then I remembered why I was there. My coach and I spoke, and he told me to go to the restroom and take a deep breath without thinking about anything for a couple of minutes. Then I told myself, “Sandra, the tournament is not over. Forget the first three games and play the next one.” So I reset. I focused on one game at a time, and I started winning. That comeback showed me that resilience is everything in chess. You can have a bad start, but you don’t have to finish badly.

Take us through the moment you realised you had won the title. What emotions went through you?

It felt surreal. At first, I was in disbelief, then pure joy and relief hit me all at once.The moment I realised I had won, the first thing I did was look up and thank God. I immediately thought of my family, my coach and everyone in Nigeria who believed in me. All the early mornings, the losses and the sacrifices — it all made sense in that moment. It was a mix of fulfilment and motivation — fulfilment because the hard work paid off, and motivation because I knew this was just the beginning. Most of all, I felt so proud to raise the Nigerian flag and bring the title home.

How has the World Amateur title changed your confidence ahead of the Chess Olympiad?

 It changed how I see myself. Before, I was just “a player with potential.” Now I know I can compete and win at the world level. My ambitions have become bigger. In the short term, I want to achieve title norms. In the long term, I want to become a Grandmaster and help Nigeria win at the Olympiad. I believe this is just the beginning.

What are your biggest ambitions in chess and beyond the game?

My biggest goal is to become a Grandmaster. I want to keep representing Nigeria and Africa on the world stage and make my country proud. Outside of chess, I want to become a medical doctor. I want to help people and give back to my community. I also want to inspire more young girls to pick up chess. I want them to see that it doesn’t matter where you start — from the streets, from school or from anywhere. You can get to the top. With God, hard work and resilience, I believe I can achieve both my dreams in chess and in medicine. I’m not done yet. This is just the beginning.

content:
The Transmission Company of Nigeria has announced a five-hour power outage in Bida and surrounding communities in Niger State to enable it to carry out annual preventive maintenance at its Bida 132/33kV Transmission Substation.

TCN said the maintenance exercise would take place on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, between 8 a.m. and 1 p.m.

According to the company in a post on its X handle on Wednesday, its maintenance crew will carry out preventive work on a 60MVA 132/33kV transformer and associated switchgear at the substation.

The exercise will affect electricity supply to several communities served by the Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC).

“Affected areas include Bida Town, Army Barracks, Agaie, Doko, Baro, Zago, Emi Rani, Bussu, Laugba Goshigi, Lafiyagi Essa, Amgulu, Mansantali, Agaie Town, Low Cost and Masaga, as well as surrounding villages,” the post read.

TCN said power supply would be restored to the affected areas upon completion of the maintenance exercise.

The company apologised to electricity customers in the affected communities for the inconvenience caused by the planned outage.

The maintenance is part of TCN’s preventive maintenance programme aimed at improving the reliability and stability of electricity transmission infrastructure.

content:
The Anambra State Government has challenged former Governor Peter Obi’s claim that he left more than ₦2.13bn in an ecological fund account before leaving office in 2014, saying the First Bank account he identified was not an ecological fund account and had never contained the amount he cited.

The state Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Law Mefor, said this in a statement shared on Wednesday by the Anambra New Media X account, titled, “Gov Peter Obi and Record of Public Debt in Anambra: Facts Beyond Propaganda and Lies.”

Mefor said the government had obtained a certified printout of the First Bank account, number 2018779464, identified by Obi as the account where he left the ecological funds.

He said, “We have obtained a certified printout of the account from inception to date. The account is an Internally Generated Revenue Consolidated Revenue Account, not an ecological fund account.”

 “From 2011 when the account was opened until date, there has never been any such amount—whether as inflow or balance—in the account.”

The commissioner consequently asked Obi to explain where the ₦2.13bn he claimed to have left for his successor was kept.

The latest response followed Obi’s Tuesday statement rejecting claims by the Anambra Government that his administration left behind inherited debts, including a ₦2bn ecological loan, contractor liabilities and unpaid salaries, gratuities and pensions.

Obi had said his administration systematically liquidated historical gratuities and arrears dating back several years, amounting to more than ₦35bn.

“At the point of handover, the state owed nothing in salaries, gratuities, or pensions, nor did we owe anything to any contractor for projects duly executed and certified,” he said.

On the disputed ecological fund, Obi said the money was released barely three months before the end of his tenure for the Oko/Umuchiana erosion crisis.

Obi said that despite pressure to spend the money, he refused, insisting that it should be left for his successor because “government is a continuum” and the funds were tied to a specific project.

He further claimed that the money was left “100 per cent intact” in First Bank, with the account balance standing at more than ₦2.13bn.

But responding to the claim, Mefor said the government’s certified printout of the account from its inception to date did not support Obi’s description of the account or the amount he claimed.

The commissioner also addressed the wider issue of debts allegedly inherited by the current administration, saying eight external borrowings remained after Obi left office on March 17, 2014.

According to Mefor, “as of June 30, 2026, the total balance of these loans stood at ₦127.4 billion at the official exchange rate.”

The loans listed by the government included the Malaria Control Booster Project, Third National Fadama Development Project, Health System Development Project II, State Education Programme Investment Project, Community and Social Development Project, Nigeria Erosion and Watershed Management Project and Value Chain Development Project.

Mefor also disputed Obi’s claim that his administration left office without owing salaries, gratuities or pensions.

He said the Soludo administration had cleared about ₦22bn in inherited gratuity arrears, but added that “legacy arrears remain from Obi and earlier administrations.”

According to him, the outstanding liabilities included arrears involving retired teachers and staff of the Water Corporation.

On the Water Corporation workers, Mefor said, “salary arrears lingered through the Obi administration and were eventually settled under the Soludo administration, with the first two of three instalments already paid.”

He further said Obi’s administration verified and certified 16 months of salary arrears for primary school teachers but paid only five months.

Mefor said, “The Obi administration verified/certified 16 months of salary arrears for primary school teachers but paid only five months.”

The commissioner also rejected Obi’s claim that his administration left more than ₦75bn in savings.

Mefor said, “We will not engage in nebulous creative accounting. If there were ₦75 billion in savings, as claimed, where are the records?”

The government’s response came after Obi rejected the debt claims and challenged anyone who could establish that his account of the ecological fund was false.

“If anybody can establish anything to the contrary, I will stop campaigning,” Obi said.

content:
Two women have been killed in India’s northeastern state of Manipur, police said Wednesday, taking the number of civilian casualties due to ethnic strife there to 10 in the last three weeks.

Unrest has flared between far-flung Manipur’s predominantly Hindu Meitei majority and its mainly Christian Kuki minority since 2023, but the violence has spread in recent months and drawn in the Naga group.

The conflict, fuelled by competing claims over land and political influence, has claimed more than 250 lives.

The two women were killed near their home in Tamenglong district, around 150 kilometres (90 miles) west of the state capital Imphal.

“There is an ongoing shutdown in Tamenglong because of the killing of two women… on Tuesday afternoon,” police superintendent Lanmiyo Luikham told AFP.

Luikham said the attack appeared to be linked to recent clashes between mainly Christian Naga and Kuki groups.

“We are carrying out the investigation and necessary formalities, and focusing on maintaining calm in the region,” he said.

The attack comes days after eight people were killed in three separate incidents across the state, which shares a porous border with war-torn Myanmar.

Efforts by the Indian government to restore normalcy have had little success.

content:
The Chairman of the Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission, Dr Muhammed Shehu, has commended Governor Alex Otti for the prudent management of Abia State’s resources.

Shehu gave the commendation on Tuesday when he and members of the commission paid a courtesy visit to Governor Otti at the governor’s Nvosi office in Isiala Ngwa South Local Government Area of the state.

He said Otti’s achievements were evidence of his prudent management of the state’s resources, particularly his massive investments in road infrastructure and education, among others, which he said had significantly impacted the state.

Shehu said, “I am so glad that today I am able to make it, to see you here and to see all the developmental strides that you have taken and are still undertaking since you assumed office as the Executive Governor of this state.

“I wouldn’t hesitate to say that this state is blessed to have you as Governor. Every independent analyst will testify that this is the best, if not the best-governed state in Nigeria, and you are certainly the best among all those who have governed the state.”

The RMAFC chairman also acknowledged Otti’s efforts in primary healthcare, fiscal transparency and security, noting that the state’s improved fiscal performance and peaceful environment were indications of responsible governance.

He cited the state’s movement from 17th to fourth position in fiscal transparency, as well as the reduction in its debt profile, as significant achievements.

Shehu appreciated Governor Otti for supporting RMAFC in its efforts to strengthen its operations and fulfil its constitutional mandate, particularly through the provision of land for the construction of the commission’s office in the state.

The chairman disclosed that the commission was undergoing reforms aimed at strengthening revenue monitoring, enhancing digitalisation and improving real-time access to revenue information from revenue-generating agencies.

He added that the commission was also working on a new revenue allocation formula, noting that the existing formula had been in operation for several decades and needed to reflect the changing responsibilities of the three tiers of government.

According to him, the review had become necessary because states now had greater responsibilities, including expanded roles in areas such as transportation infrastructure and other sectors previously dominated by the Federal Government.

He said steps were being taken to ensure that funds meant for development were recovered and appropriately distributed and utilised.

Shehu also expressed appreciation to Otti for granting the commission land for its permanent office in Abia, assuring that the building, when completed, would conform to the commission’s standard across the country.

Responding, Governor Otti said the state was pleased with the commission’s proposed reforms, expressing optimism that they would empower states to do more for their people.

He said, “We are very happy that you are doing what you are doing there. And we know that with the changes that you are proposing, and with the President supporting us, we know we can, as stated, be more empowered.

“If states are more empowered, they will do a lot more good for these states.”

Otti reassured RMAFC of his continued support to enable it to succeed and expressed hope that the proposed new revenue allocation formula would be implemented soon to allow states to do more for their people.

content:
Four people were reported dead on Wednesday following a fatal crash that occurred at about 4 a.m. around Straight Gate School, Ipara Remo, along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

The crash involved a blue Mitsubishi Canter with registration number FGE 753 XA and an ash-coloured HOWO truck with registration number T-695 KT.

The crash was reportedly caused by speeding, fatigue and wrongful overtaking.

The Mitsubishi driver, who was reportedly travelling at high speed, rammed into the moving truck while attempting to overtake.

Fatigue was also identified as a contributing factor, as the driver was reportedly fatigued during the journey.

The spokesperson for the Ogun State Sector Command of the Federal Road Safety Corps, Chief Route Commander Afolabi Odunsi, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists on Wednesday.

Odunsi said, “The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Ogun State Sector Command, confirmed a fatal road traffic crash that occurred at about 0400hrs on Wednesday, 16 September 2026, along the Ibadan–Lagos route at Straight Gate.

“A total of eight (8) persons were involved in the crash. Four (4) persons, all male adults, were killed, while one (1) male adult sustained injuries and three (3) persons were unhurt.

“Two vehicles were involved in the crash: Mitsubishi Cabstar, blue in colour, registration number FGE 753 XA. HOWO Truck, ash in colour, registration number T-695 KT.

“Preliminary investigation indicates that the crash was caused by speed violation (SPV) and wrong overtaking (WOV). The Mitsubishi driver, reportedly travelling at high speed, rammed into the moving truck while attempting to overtake. Fatigue was also identified as a contributing factor, as the driver was reportedly fatigued during the journey.”

He said the FRSC rescue team received the report at 4:33 a.m. and arrived at the scene at 4:39 a.m., recording a six-minute response time.

Odunsi said the injured victim was taken to Victory Hospital, Ogere, for medical attention, while the bodies of the deceased were deposited at the FOS Mortuary, Ipara.

He added that the crashed vehicles had been handed over to the Police Motor Traffic Division, Isara Division, for further investigation and necessary action.

Meanwhile, the Ogun State Sector Commander, Corps Commander Oludare Ogunjobi, urged motorists to avoid speeding, fatigue and unsafe overtaking, especially during early-morning journeys.

Drivers were also advised to take adequate rest before embarking on long-distance trips and to overtake only when it was safe and permissible to do so.

content:
The Ondo State Government has announced a ban on the operation of commercial motorcycles, popularly known as okadas, on some routes in Akure, the state capital.

The government said the move was aimed at improving traffic management in the state.

The Special Adviser to Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa on Transport, Olumuyiwa Ogunyemi, who spoke with journalists in Akure on Tuesday, said the government was ready to prosecute motorists, commercial motorcycle riders and other road users who violated traffic regulations, particularly traffic light signals.

He said the enforcement was part of measures to improve traffic management in Akure and other parts of the state.

Ogunyemi explained that motorcycle operators would only be allowed to operate up to designated points within the affected areas.

He said, “Okada operations have been banned on some routes in Akure. Riders approaching from the Police Officers’ Mess route will be restricted to approved locations, while those coming through the First Bank area in Alagbaka will terminate their operations around the Teaching Service Commission axis in Akure.”

He said the government would intensify enforcement of traffic laws following ongoing public enlightenment campaigns aimed at preparing residents for changes in the traffic landscape occasioned by new infrastructure projects, including the ongoing flyover construction in the state capital.

The governor’s aide emphasised that road users must begin to adapt to modern traffic management systems, including strict compliance with traffic lights and designated bus stops.

“The people living in the state capital should know that it is no longer business as usual. They must obey traffic lights and traffic regulations. We want to ensure that we do more on enforcement, having already commenced sensitisation and enlightenment for road users,” he said.

He also warned that commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators who ignored traffic signals would face arrest and prosecution.

“We have noticed that Okada riders and tricycle operators often fail to wait for the green signal before moving. Such behaviour will not be tolerated. Anyone who violates traffic regulations will be arrested and prosecuted,” Ogunyemi stated.

The Special Adviser urged residents to cooperate with the government’s efforts to modernise the transportation infrastructure and ensure the free flow of traffic across the state capital.

He noted that additional traffic management facilities, including zebra crossings and speed limit signs, would be installed, particularly around schools and other sensitive locations, to improve road safety.

“People should cooperate with the government to allow the free flow of traffic. The government is doing everything possible to make the state capital a better place,” he said.

title: UK inflation jumps to 3.1% in August as fuel prices rise

Britain’s annual inflation rate climbed in line with analysts’ expectations in August, official data showed Wednesday, as the Middle East war drove up fuel prices.

content:
Britain’s annual inflation rate climbed in line with analysts’ expectations in August, official data showed Wednesday, as the Middle East war drove up fuel prices.

The Consumer Prices Index rose 3.1 per cent in the 12 months to August, up from 2.9 per cent the previous month, the Office for National Statistics said.

Higher inflation adds pressure on Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his finance minister John Healey to ease the cost of living for households ahead of the Labour government’s budget update next month.

The Bank of England is forecast to maintain its benchmark interest rate at 3.75 percent on Thursday as the UK economy struggles for growth.

To tackle persistently high consumer prices, the US Federal Reserve is expected Wednesday to also lift borrowing costs, following a similar move by the European Central Bank last week.

With central bank interest rates on the rise — and government bond yields reaching multi-decade highs in recent weeks — Healey has pledged to maintain strict fiscal discipline.

But he has not been drawn on whether this means his budget on October 28 will include new tax rises.

Analysts expect inflation to rise towards the end of the year as higher energy costs feed through to bills further, with little sign of a deal to end the Middle East war.

“With the situation in the Middle East looking increasingly fraught, the expectation is that inflation will continue to climb higher until the end of the year at a minimum,” said Richard Carter, head of fixed interest research at Quilter Cheviot.

“For the government, today’s figures are a kick in the teeth for an administration that wants to make easing the cost of living its central mission,” he added.

content:
The 2026/27 Premier League season began on Friday, August 21, with champions Arsenal hosting newly promoted Coventry City, and the campaign is scheduled to conclude on Sunday, May 30, 2027. The 380-match season comprises 33 weekends and five midweek rounds.

After four matchweeks, the early picture is already taking shape, with Arsenal and Manchester City maintaining perfect starts while seven teams remain unbeaten.

At the other end, five clubs are still searching for their first victory, while Tottenham and Coventry are yet to score.

The next round begins on Friday, September 18, with Brentford hosting Chelsea, before the final fixtures of Matchweek 5 are played on September 20.

That round will be the last before the Premier League’s first international break of the season, which begins on September 21 and runs until October 6. The 16-day window, covering four international matches and combining the traditional September and October windows, is the first of its kind in the current Premier League calendar.

20 talking points from the Premier League so far:

1. Arsenal, Man City perfect after four games

Arsenal and Manchester City are the only two sides with four wins from four, giving both 12 points.

2. Seven teams remain unbeaten

Arsenal, Manchester City, Leeds United, Hull City, Brentford, Liverpool and Everton have yet to lose after four matches.

3. Five teams are still without a win

Bournemouth, Tottenham, Fulham, Aston Villa and Coventry City are yet to record a victory.

4. Brighton have scored 13 goals

Brighton are the division’s highest-scoring side after four matches, with 13 goals.

5. Arsenal have conceded just once

Arsenal have the league’s best defensive record, conceding only one goal in their opening four matches.

6. Leeds rise to third after Newcastle rout

Leeds moved into third place on eight points after beating Newcastle United 4-1 at Elland Road.

7. Hull are unbeaten among the promoted sides

Hull City have won two and drawn two, leaving them fourth on eight points after four games.

8. Brentford, Liverpool and Everton share six points

The three clubs have identical records of one win and three draws.

9. Tottenham and Coventry are yet to score

Both clubs have played four matches without finding the net.

10. Coventry are bottom without a point

The promoted side have lost all four games, scoring none and conceding 10.

11. Haaland leads the scoring chart

Erling Haaland has four goals. Bruno Fernandes, Alexander Isak, Bukayo Saka, Kevin Schade, Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Marcus Tavernier have three each.

12. Four players lead the assists chart

Cody Gakpo, Daichi Kamada, Evanilson and Joao Pedro have three assists each after four matches.

13. Chelsea have seven points despite conceding nine

Chelsea have two wins, one draw and one defeat, but have already conceded nine goals.

14. Manchester United sit 13th

United have one win, one draw and two defeats, leaving them on four points after four matches. In fact, they are two points above Spurs who are yet to score or win a game.

15. Ipswich have six points despite a negative goal difference

Ipswich have won two and lost two, giving them six points despite scoring seven and conceding 10.

16. Raya and Tzolakis lead the clean-sheet chart

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya and Hull goalkeeper Kostas Tzolakis have each kept three clean sheets.

17. Five red cards have been shown

Five players have been sent off so far — João Gomes (Aston Villa), Phil Foden (Manchester City), Taiwo Awoniyi (Coventry City), Axel Disasi (Crystal Palace) and Reinildo Mandava (Sunderland) — with Aston Villa, Manchester City, Coventry City, Crystal Palace and Sunderland each having one red card, according to My Football Facts.

18. Bournemouth and Hull lead yellow-card count

Bournemouth and Hull City have picked up the most yellow cards after four matches, with 13 each, followed by Nottingham Forest with 11, Statmuse reported.

19. VAR errors already feature in early-season talking points

Pro Ref admitted an “error of judgment” over Erling Haaland’s winning goal in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory over Manchester United, with chief refereeing officer Howard Webb saying “tunnel vision” led VAR officials to focus on Haaland’s position while overlooking Enzo Fernández’s potential impact from an offside position.

Reuters reported that the VAR officials involved were subsequently stood down until after the international break.

The Premier League’s own Match Centre has also published Key Match Incidents findings, including a ruling that Newcastle should have been awarded a penalty against Leeds after a challenge on Bruno Guimarães, with VAR judged to have missed the opportunity to intervene, Al Jazeera reported.

20. Chelsea’s clean-sheet drought stretches to 20 league games

Chelsea have gone 20 consecutive Premier League matches without keeping a clean sheet, their longest such run in 65 years, after conceding twice in their 2-2 draw with Hull City.

PUNCH Online reports that the last time Chelsea played a clean sheet in the league was at Stamford Bridge in January 2026 in a 2-0 win over Brentford.

The First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, has given N20m to Maryam Ibrahim Dan’Azumi, who recently won the King Abdulaziz International Qur’anic Competition in Saudi Arabia.

Her elder sister, Hajara Ibrahim Dan-Azumi, won the 18th Hashemite Jordan International Qur’anic Competition for Females in Jordan in 2024.

title: UCH health workers begin indefinite strike over director’s reinstatement
description: The Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals, University College Hospital, Ibadan chapter, has commenced an indefinite strike over the alleged refusal of the hospital management to implement the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare’s recommendation on the disciplinary case involving th
content:
The Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals, University College Hospital, Ibadan chapter, has commenced an indefinite strike over the alleged refusal of the hospital management to implement the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare’s recommendation on the disciplinary case involving the Director of Pharmaceutical Services, Dr Adeyinka Ishola.

The union announced the industrial action in a letter addressed to members at the hospital saying it would commence on Today, Wednesday, September 16, 2026, following what it described as the failure of several efforts to resolve the dispute.

The dispute centres on the sale of a tricycle donated to the Pharmacy Department and the subsequent disciplinary action taken against Ishola.

The NUAHP Chairman, Oladayo Olabampe, said the union was demanding the implementation of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare’s recommendation that Ishola be reprimanded and reinstated.

Olabampe said an initial investigation conducted by the hospital had recommended that Ishola be suspended, with the recommendation forwarded to the ministry for ratification.

He said the ministry subsequently sent an independent investigative team to the hospital, which reached a different conclusion.

“The ministry, in its wisdom, sent a team of investigators to UCH to conduct an independent investigation. The panel found Dr Ishola not guilty of any fraudulent act but only guilty of not carrying the management along in the sale of the tricycle,” he said.

He added, “Rather than approving the dismissal recommended by UCH, the ministry, after a thorough investigation, recommended that the director be reprimanded and then reinstated.”

The union chairman accused the hospital management of refusing to implement the recommendation despite the ministry being its supervisory authority.

“We are, however, surprised that the UCH management is not pleased with this outcome and has, for months, refused to implement the verdict of its supervisory ministry,” Olabampe said.

He said the union disagreed with the position of the hospital management that the ministry’s decision was not final.

“We hold a contrary view to that of the management of UCH, which believes that the verdict of the ministry is not final,” he said.

Defending Ishola, Olabampe said the union did not believe the sale of the tricycle amounted to fraud.

“We hereby declare that Dr Adeyinka Ishola is not a thief, though he might have committed an administrative error by not carrying the management along. Since the ministry has decided that he be reprimanded, we stand by this decision,” he said.

The NUAHP chairman said the union had exhausted its attempts at resolving the matter through dialogue.

“Having dialogued with the management on several occasions to no avail, we have hereby resolved to declare a trade dispute over this matter,” he said.

“After two series of ultimatums, we have decided to mobilise our members for an indefinite strike with effect from Wednesday, September 16, 2026. The strike shall continue until our demands are met,” Olabampe added.

Ishola was removed from office more than a year ago following an allegation that he sold the tricycle without the knowledge of UCH management.

The tricycle was reportedly donated by a pharmaceutical company. Ishola was said to have told the hospital’s investigative panel that the item was initially a personal gift to him from the company, which he subsequently handed over to the Pharmacy Department.

He reportedly challenged the panel to seek clarification from the donor company on the circumstances surrounding the donation.

Ishola was also quoted as explaining that he decided to sell the tricycle after discovering that its maintenance could be difficult because spare parts might not be readily available, as it was a fabricated model rather than the conventional type commonly used for commercial purposes.

He further explained that the N1.3m proceeds from the sale were used to address various needs of the department, including replacing trolley tyres and laptop batteries and providing office chairs for some offices.

According to his account, the proceeds were fully accounted for, with relevant documents presented to the investigative panel.

The controversy over the ownership and disposal of the tricycle has, however, remained at the centre of the dispute, with the hospital management reportedly maintaining that the item became hospital property after Ishola handed it over to the Pharmacy Department.

The latest industrial action comes amid previous labour disputes at UCH. In March 2026, workers under the Council of UCH Union Leaders embarked on a five-day warning strike over alleged electricity rationing at the hospital, with the unions citing its impact on surgeries, laboratory services and other clinical operations.

The latest dispute could further disrupt services at the tertiary institution, which serves as a major referral and training centre for patients and health professionals in the region.

title: UNFPA educates youths with disabilities on gender-based violence in Sokoto
description:

content:
The United Nations Population Fund Youth Participatory Platform (UNFPA-YPP), Sokoto State, has sensitised adolescents and young people with disabilities on sexual and reproductive health rights, gender-based violence prevention, positive masculinity and menstrual hygiene.

The programme, organised in collaboration with Taimako Inclusive Development Initiative (TIDI) and the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPWD), was held at the Sokoto South Conference Hall on Tuesday

The awareness session provided participants with information on their health, rights, safety and wellbeing, while creating a platform for them to ask questions and discuss challenges affecting young people with disabilities.

Speaking during the programme, the UNFPA-YPP PWD Desk Officer, Maimunatu Salihu, said the initiative was aimed at ensuring that disability did not become a barrier to accessing healthcare, accurate information, protection and opportunities.

Salihu said, “The essence of the programme is to create awareness among adolescents and young people with disabilities on issues that directly affect their health, rights, safety and overall wellbeing.”

She added that the session was designed as a safe space where participants could interact, share experiences and learn from one another.

Also speaking, the Chairperson of UNFPA-YPP Sokoto, Hamidu Almustapha, stressed the importance of involving young people in programmes and decisions that affect their lives.

He said youths should not merely be treated as beneficiaries but should be allowed to identify challenges, propose solutions and contribute to development activities.

Almustapha further emphasised the need for the inclusion of persons with disabilities in development programmes, saying they had equal rights to information, participation, dignity, safety and opportunities.

During a presentation on positive masculinity, Salihu explained that societal and cultural expectations could sometimes discourage boys from expressing their emotions or seeking assistance when facing difficulties.

She urged parents and caregivers to provide boys with care, affection, protection and emotional support, stressing that such support would contribute to their emotional and social development.

She also encouraged young men to reject the notion that masculinity should be associated with aggression, dominance or violence.

Instead, she advocated respect, empathy, responsibility, self-control, equality and peaceful communication as positive values that could promote healthier relationships and safer communities.

The UNFPA-YPP Co-Chair, Aisha Muhammad, linked positive masculinity to the prevention of gender-based violence, urging participants to challenge harmful stereotypes and behaviours that could contribute to violence.

Facilitating the session on gender-based violence, Muhammad explained that GBV could manifest through physical, sexual, emotional and psychological abuse.

She said persons with disabilities could face additional barriers in accessing protection and reporting abuse, making disability-inclusive support systems necessary.

“Everyone, including adolescents and young people with disabilities, has the right to live in an environment free from violence, abuse, exploitation and discrimination,” she said.

Muhammad urged participants not to normalise violence or remain silent when abuse occurs, advising them to seek assistance from trusted persons and appropriate service providers.

Menstrual hygiene

A UNICEF peer educator, Comrade Nafiu Umar Muhammad, who spoke on menstrual hygiene, described menstruation as a normal biological process that should not be surrounded by shame or stigma.

He stressed the importance of access to accurate information, menstrual materials, clean water and sanitation facilities to enable girls and young women to manage menstruation with dignity.

Muhammad also called for menstrual health information and facilities to be made accessible to young people with disabilities.

He urged participants to help dispel myths and misconceptions surrounding menstruation and encourage open discussions on menstrual health.

The programme also featured an interactive session during which participants asked questions and discussed challenges associated with accessing health information and services, cultural expectations, violence, discrimination and inclusion.

In his vote of thanks, the Secretary of the association, Mukhtar Doki, commended UNFPA-YPP, TIDI, JONAPWD and the facilitators for organising the programme.

Doki encouraged participants to share the knowledge gained with their peers and communities.

He said the programme’s impact would be enhanced if participants became “ambassadors” of the knowledge and positive messages received during the session.

The organisers subsequently called for regular sensitisation programmes on sexual and reproductive health rights, GBV prevention, positive masculinity and menstrual hygiene, as well as increased participation of young people with disabilities in advocacy and decision-making processes.

title: Africhange vs LemFi vs NALA: Which UK Remittance App Should You Switch To?
description:
If you regularly send money from the UK to Nigeria, you don’t necessarily have to stick with one remittance app.
You can have Africhange, LemFi, and NALA on the same phone, enter £500 into each, and compare how much your recipient would get. But the exchange rate is only one factor in the decision,
content:
If you regularly send money from the UK to Nigeria, you don’t necessarily have to stick with one remittance app.

You can have Africhange, LemFi, and NALA on the same phone, enter £500 into each, and compare how much your recipient would get. But the exchange rate is only one factor in the decision, especially if you send money regularly.

One provider may offer a better rate today but have a shorter operating history, while another may have millions of customers and a product you already trust, but leave you with slightly less naira on a particular transfer. There are also differences in fees, support, and what you can do with the app besides sending money to Nigeria.

We’ve compared all three on the same criteria: rates and fees, track record, transfer speed and reliability, customer reviews, and additional features.

1. Rates and fees

Rates are probably the first thing to compare because a difference of a few naira per pound becomes more noticeable as the amount you send increases.

The problem with checking rates once is that they move throughout the day. The provider offering the most naira for £500 this morning may not still be ahead tomorrow.

There is, however, a sizeable historical dataset comparing Africhange and LemFi.

Earlier this month, Africhange published an analysis of historical exchange-rate records sourced from BestRates. The study covered January 2025 to August 2026 and matched Africhange and LemFi quotes captured at similar times.

Across 37,521 observations matched within ten minutes, Africhange had the higher GBP-to-NGN quote 91.8% of the time. LemFi was higher in 4.4%, while 3.8% of the observations were equal.

The average difference across the dataset was ₦12.69 per £1 in Africhange’s favour, with a median difference of ₦10. Africhange also had a positive average rate difference in each of the 20 months covered by the study.

For NALA, we have a much narrower comparison. When we checked BestRates while preparing this article, a £100 transfer showed Africhange at ₦1,845 per pound and NALA at ₦1,842.84. That worked out to ₦184,500 through Africhange and ₦184,284.10 through NALA, a difference of roughly ₦216.

Fees are another point of difference. Africhange and LemFi do not charge a separate transfer fee on UK-to-Nigeria transfers, so the main thing to compare between them is the exchange rate and, ultimately, how much naira the recipient gets. NALA currently charges £0.99 for bank transfers to Nigeria, while mobile-money transfers have no separate transfer fee apart from the margin built into its exchange rate.

Based on the available evidence, Africhange has a strong historical rate case against LemFi. Across the 37,521 matched observations in its BestRates analysis, it offered the higher quoted rate 91.8% of the time. There is not enough long-term data to make a meaningful comparison between Africhange and NALA, so the live payout remains the most useful way to compare the two before sending.

2. Track record and scale

Based on the latest customer figures disclosed by the companies, LemFi has the largest reported customer base of the three. Its current website claims it is trusted by more than 2 million users, while NALA says it is trusted by more than 1 million people across 35+ countries. These are company-reported global figures, rather than UK-to-Nigeria customer numbers.

LemFi has also disclosed more about the volume of money moving through its platform. TechCrunch reported in January 2025 that the company was processing around $1 billion in payments each month. At the time, LemFi had more than one million active customers and had just raised a $53 million Series B, bringing its total disclosed funding to $85 million.

That scale gives LemFi a larger disclosed operating base, but it does not necessarily translate into a better rate, lower cost, or better experience for someone sending money to Nigeria today. NALA has also grown considerably. Its current website says it is trusted by more than one million people in 35+ countries. We did not find a directly comparable current monthly transaction-volume figure from NALA, so LemFi’s $1 billion figure should not be interpreted as proof that its entire business is necessarily larger.

Africhange has the shortest UK operating history of the three. TechCabal reported in November 2024 that it had more than 200,000 users globally and had processed more than two million transactions since launch. Those figures measure something different from LemFi’s current customer count and monthly payment volume, so putting them side by side does not give us a clean measure of relative scale.

A shorter operating history or smaller reported customer base does not automatically mean poorer service, just as having more customers does not guarantee better value. But for someone who places a lot of weight on the amount of publicly disclosed operating history behind a remittance provider, LemFi currently provides more evidence to examine.

3. Transfer speed and reliability

Speed is one of the harder categories to rank fairly.

NALA says most transfers to Nigeria are instant or arrive within a few minutes. Its published transfer times vary according to how the recipient receives the money.

LemFi also markets its transfers as fast, while Africhange is built around near-instant cross-border transfers. The problem is that the providers do not publish their figures using the same methodology.

Transfers can also take longer because of verification, compliance checks, or third-party processing by the recipient’s financial institution.

For that reason, we don’t think the available evidence supports naming a speed winner among the three. All are designed to deliver digital remittances quickly, and there is no comparable independent test showing that one consistently completes UK-to-Nigeria transfers faster than the others.

4. Customer reviews and support

Support is similarly difficult to turn into a clean ranking because none of the three publishes comparable UK-to-Nigeria resolution or failure rates.

Public reviews give us more to work with, though they must be treated carefully. Trustpilot reviews can come from customers in different countries and use different transfer corridors, so they are better for identifying recurring customer experiences than for calculating which provider is objectively more reliable.

LemFi has by far the largest public review footprint of the three. Its Trustpilot profile has tens of thousands of reviews, with positive feedback frequently highlighting ease of use and successful transfers. Complaints include transfers that remain pending and difficulties in resolving more complex cases.

NALA has a considerably smaller review base. Its reviews also include plenty of positive experiences alongside complaints about delayed or failed transactions and the time it takes to resolve individual problems.

Africhange has the smallest review footprint of the three. Customers have praised support and successful transfers, while negative reviews cite issues with verification, funding, and transfer delays.

Those patterns are not unusual for remittance services, and the review data is not clean enough to declare a support winner.

5. What else can you do with each app?

All three companies are expanding beyond the basic act of converting Pounds to Naira, and there is more overlap among their products than might initially appear.

Africhange offers eligible UK customers GBP accounts through Griffin, each with its own sort code and account number. Customers can receive payments, hold GBP, and make transfers using Faster Payments. Griffin also says eligible deposits are protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS). Africhange supports multiple currencies as well and offers volume-based rate improvements for qualifying transfers.

LemFi also offers multi-currency functionality. UK users can hold and manage multiple currencies, while its broader UK product has expanded to include an instant-access savings account. Its current UK site also lists credit, credit monitoring, and other financial products, although eligibility and availability vary.

So multi-currency accounts are not, by themselves, a meaningful distinction between LemFi and Africhange. The differences are more specific. Africhange combines its remittance service with UK bank account functionality through Griffin and volume-based rate improvements, while LemFi has expanded further into products such as savings and credit-related services.

NALA is developing its own Global Account proposition. Its main website describes functionality for receiving, holding, converting, and sending money across borders. There is some nuance around availability, however. NALA’s August 2026 Global Accounts terms specifically describe its USD Global Account as a service for receiving cross-border USD payments, holding USD value and, where available, converting and withdrawing into local currency. We therefore would not assume every Global Account feature shown on NALA’s wider site is available to every UK customer.

All three are moving beyond simple remittances, but in somewhat different directions. That makes the individual features you would actually use more useful for comparison than describing any one of the three as having the “broader” product.

So, Africhange, LemFi or NALA?

There isn’t one answer that works for everyone.

If your priority is the GBP-to-NGN exchange rate, Africhange has the strongest historical evidence we found against LemFi. Across more than 37,000 matched observations, its quoted rate was higher 91.8% of the time. That is meaningful evidence, even after accounting for the fact that Africhange conducted the analysis itself.

If you put more weight on track record and scale, specifically in the UK, LemFi makes the stronger case. It had already surpassed one million active customers and was processing around $1 billion per month by early 2025. Existing LemFi customers also have their own transaction history to consider. If you have used it reliably for years, a small difference in rate may not be enough to make you switch.

NALA becomes more interesting if you want a product built to manage money across borders, rather than just sending money to Nigeria. Its Global Account proposition and reach across more than 35 countries give it a broader international focus, although the availability of individual account features can vary.

Speed does not give us a convincing reason to choose one over the others, and the public support data is not comparable enough to crown a winner there either.

For a regular UK-to-Nigeria sender, that leaves a fairly practical decision. Check how much naira each app will deliver for the amount you want to send, make sure you are comparing standard pricing rather than a temporary welcome offer, and then weigh that against your experience with the provider and any additional financial features you actually intend to use.

Based on the available evidence, Africhange is particularly worth comparing if the rate is your priority, LemFi if operating history and scale matter more, and NALA if you want a broader cross-border account product.

Those are reasons to consider each provider, rather than reasons to assume any one of them will be the best choice every time.

title: Man Utd, Villa target last 16 as Carabao Cup draw holds Wednesday night
description:

content:
The Carabao Cup fourth-round draw will take place on Wednesday night, with 11 clubs already assured of places and five spots still to be settled.

The draw is scheduled to be conducted shortly after Manchester United’s third-round clash with Brighton, with Pien Meulensteen hosting the proceedings and former Liverpool midfielder Jamie Redknapp and former Aston Villa captain Ashley Young drawing the balls.

Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Newcastle United, Chelsea and Bradford City had already secured their places in the fourth round after winning their respective third-round ties.

Five more teams joined them on Tuesday, with Arsenal, Liverpool, Fulham, Brentford and Peterborough United progressing.

Arsenal booked their place with a 4-2 victory away to Ipswich Town, while Liverpool advanced after beating Tottenham Hotspur 3-1.

Fulham defeated West Ham United 3-2, Brentford edged Reading 2-1 and Peterborough United progressed on penalties after a 3-3 draw with Barnsley.

Four more third-round ties will be played on Wednesday before the draw.

Everton will host Wolves, Fleetwood Town face Sheffield United, Coventry City entertain Aston Villa, while Manchester United welcome Brighton.

The final third-round tie will be played on Thursday, when defending champions Manchester City host Championship side Norwich City.

As a result, the winner of the City-Norwich tie will be represented by a placeholder in Wednesday night’s draw, with the identity of the final club to complete the 16-team line-up not known until Thursday.

The fourth-round ties are scheduled to be played in the week commencing October 26.

content:
The US federal government is on track to approve a $2.8 billion arms package for Israel, US media reported Tuesday, with the sale of 40,000 one-ton bombs among the largest munitions packages sold in recent years.

The Washington Post said the package — funded with US taxpayer dollars — featured some of the most destructive munitions in Western arsenals, including 20,000 MK-84s, 20,000 BLU-117s, and 20,000 I-2000 Penetrator warheads.

The New York Times said the administration of US President Donald Trump had approved the sale, citing a US official.

A senior administration official told AFP that “all foreign arms sales are moving through the appropriate process,” but wouldn’t comment on pending transactions.

Meanwhile, a State Department spokesperson told AFP that “as a matter of policy, the Department does not confirm or comment on proposed arms sales until they have been formally notified to Congress.”

The deal was reported amid an ongoing munitions shortage within the US military, with stocks rapidly depleting from the war with Iran and with the US spending $22.3 billion on munitions between February 28 and June 30.

In February 2025, the Trump administration had approved the sale of more than $7.4 billion in bombs, missiles and related equipment to Israel, including MK-84 munitions.

In response to concerns over civilian deaths in Gaza, former US President Joe Biden’s administration had blocked a shipment of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel, but the Trump Administration approved them after taking office in early 2025.

Motorists on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway have been trapped
content:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and All Progressives Congress governors have clashed over the Rainbow Coalition, with the governors rejecting any alliance that could undermine President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

Motorists on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway have been trapped in a 14-hour gridlock after a multiple-vehicle crash at the Kara Bridge compounded ongoing repair works.

Former Manchester United striker Andy Cole has said several factors beyond transfer fees and salaries may have prevented Premier League clubs from signing Victor Osimhen.

A man identified as Adejuwon Adekunle has been shot dead by gunmen near a recreation centre in the Dele Yes Sir community, Osogbo, Osun State.

Suspected armed herders have ambushed the entourage of the Divisional Police Officer in Ayilamo, Logo Local Government Area of Benue State, killing two police officers.

And several Nigerian football stars, including Tolu Arokodare, Kelechi Iheanacho, Gift Orban and Samuel Chukwueze, have been reviving their club careers across Europe after difficult spells at previous clubs.

Here is a recap of the major stories making headlines this morning.

1. 2027: Wike, Apc govs clash over Rainbow Coalition

APC governors, led by Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma, have rejected any alliance capable of undermining President Tinubu’s re-election or weakening the party.

Wike has defended his Rainbow Coalition, insisting it supports Tinubu while allowing the PDP to field candidates in other contests. The rivalry is linked to positioning for 2031.

Read full story: https://punchng.com/2027-wike-apc-govs-clash-over-rainbow-coalition/

2. Lagos-Ibadan: Motorists trapped in 14-hour gridlock

A crash involving seven vehicles at the Kara Bridge on Tuesday morning, combined with ongoing expansion joint repairs, left motorists stranded for more than 14 hours.

Some drivers drove against traffic, worsening the congestion that stretched into Lagos. No lives were lost in the crash.

Read full story: https://punchng.com/lagos-ibadan-motorists-trapped-in-14-hour-gridlock/

3. Why Premier League teams failed to sign Osimhen – Cole

Andy Cole has said Victor Osimhen has the quality to succeed in the Premier League but that transfers involve many factors beyond salary and fees.

The striker has been linked with Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea without a move materialising. He continues to score freely at Galatasaray.

Read full story: https://punchng.com/why-premier-league-teams-failed-to-sign-osimhen-cole/

4. Man shot dead near Osun recreation centre

Adejuwon Adekunle, popularly known as Asa, was shot by gunmen between 1:30am and 2am on Tuesday near a recreation centre in Dele Yes Sir, Osogbo.

Police say the attack is suspected to be cult-related and have transferred the case to the Criminal Investigation Department. No arrest has been made.

Read full story: https://punchng.com/man-shot-dead-near-osun-recreation-centre/

5. Suspected herders ambush Benue Dpo, kill two policemen

Suspected armed herders ambushed the Divisional Police Officer’s entourage in Ayilamo, Logo Local Government Area, on Monday evening, killing two Mobile Police officers.

The attack came barely days after another incident in the same community claimed four policemen and seven residents.

Read full story: https://punchng.com/suspected-herders-ambush-benue-dpo-kill-two-policemen/

6. Nigerian stars reviving club careers in Europe

Tolu Arokodare has scored six goals in 11 appearances for Ajax, Kelechi Iheanacho leads the Turkish first division scoring charts at Bursaspor, Gift Orban is among the Super Lig’s top scorers at Amedspor, and Samuel Chukwueze is impressing in a new wing-back role at AC Milan.

title: Experts visit site of Enugu building collapse, blame negligence

content:
Standing amid shattered concrete, exposed rebar, and scattered belongings at the site of a collapsed four-story building in the heart of Enugu, the mood on Monday was one of profound grief mixed with professional outrage.

The detached structure had violently given way on Sunday, leaving one person dead and another critically injured, while several others were rushed to hospital.

By Monday morning, executive delegations from Nigeria’s primary built-environment institutes converged on the scene for an on-the-spot forensic assessment.

What they found was a familiar, tragic story: A deadly cocktail of severe site negligence, missing regulatory frameworks and compromised construction standards.

Surveying the remains, leaders from the Nigerian Institute of Town Planners (NITP) and the Nigerian Institute of Building (NIOB) minced no words regarding the immediate visual causes of the failure.

Dr. Christopher Anierobi, Chairman, NITP, Enugu State chapter, said, “This collapse is a result of gross negligence. You can see that the material mixture is completely inadequate. There was gross negligence on the part of the site engineers and a total failure of professional supervision.”

Dr. Eucharia Enebe, Second National Vice President of the NIOB, pointed out that structural integrity fails long before concrete is poured on-site.

She emphasised that basic quality management, health and safety planning, and construction management protocols were glaringly absent.

While immediate human error triggered the structural collapse, experts at the site unanimously pointed to a deeper institutional failure: Enugu State’s reliance on obsolete planning frameworks and unapproved master plans.

Currently, urban development in Enugu is guided by an unapproved, outdated 1979 document drafted during the administration of Chief Jim Nwobodo – over four decades ago.

Anierobi and NIOB Vice State Chairman, Ani Chukwunoso urged Governor Peter Mbah to domesticate the 1992 Nigerian Urban and Regional Planning Law and the 2006 National Building Code.

According to them, doing so will empower regulatory bodies to legally restrict site supervision to certified professionals – architects, structural engineers, and registered builders – rather than non-expert inspectors treating approvals as mere revenue ventures.

Attention immediately shifted to the adjacent twin detached structure, which remains standing right beside the rubble.

Experts warned that the violent shockwave from Sunday’s collapse may have compromised its structural integrity.

Enebe said, “Because the first structure fell, it inevitably impacted the second. Full non-destructive integrity tests must be conducted before anyone can deem the remaining structure safe to occupy.”

Sunday’s tragedy comes just 24 hours after the Enugu Capital Territory Development Authority (ECTDA) issued a statement on the structure.

ECTDA officials had confirmed that while the developer had obtained structural approvals, preliminary checks revealed severe deviations from approved engineering drawings, densification violations, and unmonitored structural modifications during construction.

The ECTDA stated it had sealed the immediate perimeter, launched a full administrative inquiry, and promised that any developer or supervising official found culpable of regulatory breach would face prosecution under state laws.

As rescue operations conclude and forensic investigations begin, the message from built-environment professionals is unequivocal: condolences and post-disaster panels are no longer enough.

Without the immediate domestication of modern planning laws and strict enforcement of the National Building Code, Enugu risks repeating the tragic cycle of avoidable structural failures.
