title: 2027: Wike, APC govs clash over Rainbow Coalition
description: The growing rivalry among political actors ahead of the 2027 general elections, coupled with emerging ambitions for the 2031 presidency, has highlighted tensions between the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and governors of the All Progressives Congress, with the development t
content:
The growing rivalry among political actors ahead of the 2027 general elections, coupled with emerging ambitions for the 2031 presidency, has highlighted tensions between the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and governors of the All Progressives Congress, with the development threatening to complicate President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Wike, who is serving in the APC-led Federal Government, has been promoting a Rainbow Coalition in Rivers State to support President Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

In the late hours of Monday night, the Chairman of the APC’s Progressive Governors’ Forum and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, in an indirect attack at Wike said the ruling party governors would not support any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining the re-election of President Tinubu or weakening the party ahead of the 2027 elections.

Uzodimma maintained that the governors’ campaign commitment remained exclusively to APC candidates at all levels.

However, Wike defended his Rainbow Coalition, insisting that the alliance was aimed at supporting President Tinubu while strengthening the opposition Peoples Democratic Party against the APC in other electoral contests.

He said his support for Tinubu did not amount to supporting APC candidates across the states, stressing that he remained free to support candidates of his choice.

Meanwhile, the camp of the PDP Interim National Working Committee led by Tanimu Turaki (SAN) mocked Tinubu and the APC governors over the development, as the National Publicity Secretary, Ini Ememobong, added that the ruling party and the President would be consumed by the monster they created.

In a sharp response, the Wike-backed PDP defended the minister, describing him as a political force that could not be discarded. The party’s Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Mohammed, in an exclusive interview with our correspondent, maintained that despite Wike’s support for Tinubu at the presidential level, the PDP remained committed to fielding candidates and contesting the 2027 elections.

Wike, who has been at odds with some APC governors, alleged during a recent media chat that Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq and Governor Uzodimma were behind his political troubles in Rivers State and some other parts of the country.

According to him, the disagreement stems from the expanding influence of the Rainbow Coalition, which he said was a platform for PDP members and other politicians seeking to challenge APC candidates for governorship and senatorial seats in the 2027 elections, a development he said was at odds with the interests of the governors.

Uzodimma, at the end of the governors’ meeting in Abuja late Monday night, stressed that they had not entered into any formal agreement with any individual or opposition party ahead of the election.

In what appeared to be an indirect response to Wike’s remarks and his moves to expand his political influence across the states, the APC governors declared that they would not entertain any arrangement that could create confusion, divided loyalty or competing interests within the party.

Uzodimma, who read the communique at the end of the meeting, said the forum’s primary focus was to support official APC candidates at all levels rather than promote external interests.

He stated, “The APC Governors Forum unanimously resolved that its members will not participate in, support or endorse any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining the re-election of Mr President, weakening the APC or adversely affecting any candidate of the party at all levels.

“In other words, the forum has no intention to support any candidate at any level that is not an APC candidate because our candidates who are contesting the election are being sponsored by our party.

“The governors’ campaign commitment is exclusively to all APC candidates. All levels of the party campaign architecture will align with the expectations of Mr President and the strategic objectives of the party.”

Wike, through his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, on Tuesday reaffirmed his unwavering support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, noting that he never pledged to stop the PDP from fielding candidates in governorship, National Assembly and state assembly elections.

He clarified that the Rainbow Coalition was not affiliated to the APC but was a platform for political parties supporting Tinubu’s re-election and his administration’s achievements.

The minister noted that “politics is local and those having problems in their states should resolve them instead of using the reelection of the President to whip up sentiments.”

Wike said he never held discussions with the APC before he and other G-5 members backed President Tinubu in 2023, stressing that his support in 2027 is solely for the President.

He added that politics is no longer about finishing fourth and becoming governor, but about genuinely mobilising voters and winning elections from the polling units.

The FCT minister asked; “In Imo State, under Governor Hope Uzodinma, how did APC win two Senate seats in 2023, in an election held the same day with that of the President and APC had less than 15 per cent in the presidential election? Was it Rainbow Coalition? Were the voters confused?

“Was it Rainbow Coalition that also made APC win the National Assembly elections in Ebonyi, Abia and Enugu states where the President did not have 10 per cent of the votes?

“If in 2023, the voters in Imo, Abia, Enugu and Ebonyi voted APC in the senatorial election and voted another party in the presidential election, they won’t be confused in 2027 provided we all support the President genuinely this time?”

The minister urged all stakeholders to put the presidential election first, saying; “after the President must have been reelected, we can all go and face elections in our states.

“What I said and stand for is that I will mobilise support for the reelection of the President. I never promised anyone that PDP will not field candidates to contest governorship, National Assembly and state Houses of Assembly elections.

“Most importantly,  the Rainbow Coalition has nothing to do with the APC. Rather, it is our own way of mobilising support accross political parties for Mr President, who has done well to deserve a second term,” he said.

​Also,  Wike, in an interview on Arise TV’s Prime Time on Tuesday night, dismissed the governors’ concerns, arguing that his support for Tinubu did not mean he had abandoned the PDP.

“They (APC governors) are politically lazy. When you have your local problems, don’t use Mr President as your excuse,” Wike said.

He said the disagreements surrounding his political activities were not new, recalling that he had faced opposition from political actors while serving both as Rivers governor and FCT minister.

“This thing did not start today. It started at ministerial position. They were not happy that I was Minister of FCT. Also, they were unhappy when I was governor,” he said.

Wike also suggested that some of his critics lacked access to the information available to him on the political situation, saying they would have a different understanding of his activities if they knew what he knew.

“If they know what I know, they would not come out to shout,” he said.

The minister reiterated his support for Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that such support was separate from his activities within the PDP.

“I have said I will support the President and I am still supporting him. What has that got to do with my party?” Wike asked.

He also cited the political activities of Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo; Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke; and Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, to argue that support for a presidential candidate did not prevent political parties from fielding candidates for other elective positions.

“Take Soludo, Adeleke and Otti. Does it mean that their parties will not present other candidates? This thing they are saying does not have any basis,” he said.

Chiding AbdulRazaq, Wike said “The governor of Kwara, so unforunate. Anytime he sees a snake, it’s Wike. Any day he doesn’t eat, it’s Wike. I never see people who will give time to gossip more than the work they have been given. He has three serving senators, he changed all of them. He has House Reps, he changeed all of them.”

However, credible APC leaders, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment on the matter, said the power struggle involving Wike, Uzodimma and others was largely driven by ambitions for the 2031 presidency, political dominance and control of the 11th National Assembly.

The sources warned that unless the growing infighting among the President’s allies was addressed, it could become a major threat to President Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

One of the sources disclosed that Wike and Uzodimma were both working to expand their political influence and strengthen their positions ahead of the 2031 presidential race, particularly the vice-presidential contest.

He stated, “Wike, Uzodimma and some of them are strategising for the vice-presidential position. People have very tall ambitions. We are trying to go into the 2027 election, but people are positioning themselves for 2031 in 2026.

“The first problem was with regard to the position of each of them in relation to the President. Wike and Uzodimma have been at daggers drawn over their closeness to President Tinubu. Initially, all of them were angling for the position of Director-General of the campaign. At the end, none of them got it.

“Both men are seriously competing, and they are recruiting the President’s friends, supporters and party chieftains into their respective camps. You will recall what played out in Rivers State, where Uzodimma was supporting (Sim) Fubara and others working against Wike’s interests. In Imo State, Wike is supporting the likes of (Samuel) Anyanwu and others against Uzodimma’s interests.

“At the national level, the rivalry has also played out several times. For instance, Uzodimma and some other governors approached the President with proposals on how to raise funds for his re-election campaign. Wike subsequently went to the President and alleged that the governors were not to be trusted and could divert the funds, urging him to be cautious.

“So, this back-and-forth has been ongoing. You also recall that the Senate introduced a questionable amendment to its Standing Rules some time ago, which was later reviewed, it was done against Uzodimma’s Senate President ambition.”

He said the rivalry was largely driven by political ambitions for 2031 and control of the next National Assembly, as the actors seek to expand their influence beyond their respective states and geopolitical zones.

The source stated, “Ultimately, it is about political ambition. It is about 2031 and, of course, control of the next National Assembly. They are all trying to expand their influence beyond their respective states to their geopolitical zones and even beyond.

“You also have to understand that the APC governors have candidates to protect. Some of them are also senatorial candidates, while their parties have governorship candidates and other candidates contesting elective positions in their respective states. But Wike’s faction of the PDP is also fielding candidates, many of whom are perceived political opponents of these APC governors. Some of these politicians moved to Wike’s faction of the PDP, and the governors feel aggrieved by it.

“If you look at what is happening in Kwara State, for instance, the Saraki political dynasty is being emboldened and empowered, which could make the Kwara State governor feel threatened. The same situation is playing out in Imo, Gombe and several other states. The APC governors, under the leadership of Uzodimma, are therefore unhappy about the development.

“So, the dirty dealings are many. One person is hitting another, and the other is hitting back. Now, they are going to team up against Hope through Wike’s Rainbow Alliance. Yesterday, Hope met with the governors and they opposed the Rainbow Alliance because the alliance is principally aimed at tthwarting their interests. The whole thing is actually a fight for political positions. Hope wants to be Vice-President in 2031, and Wike also wants to be Vice-President in 2031. That is what is driving much of this rivalry.

“This infighting is also considered a threat to President Tinubu’s re-election unless he does something urgently to resolve it. If allowed to continue into the campaign period, it may affect the party and some of its candidates.”

Another APC source said the ongoing infighting was largely driven by political interests, with some governors unhappy that Wike, despite being a PDP member and serving in APC led federal cabinet, was using his influence and resources to mobilise politicians against them in various states, adding that the struggle was also part of efforts to position key actors ahead of the 2027 and 2031 elections.

He stated, “Of course, the infighting is about their political interests. Most APC governors are unhappy that Wike, a PDP member serving in an APC-led Federal Government, has been empowered by the President and is using the influence and resources available to him to mobilise politicians to contest for the State Houses of Assembly, Senate, House of Representatives and governorship positions in their respective states, mostly under the PDP, against the governors’ political interests.

“This is visible in many states, with Wike’s faction of the PDP accommodating APC members seeking to challenge serving governors. All these are part of the problem.

“Again, it is also about 2027 and 2031. Politicians plan early, and both Tinubu and Wike are positioning themselves strategically ahead of these elections so that discussions about the presidency will involve them and they can play a major role in key political decisions. It is also about the National Assembly leadership and who gets what in the next cabinet. That is probably the source of the problem.

“But we hope the President quickly swings into action and uses his influence to resolve the differences and bring them together in the interest of himself and his party. If not, it may affect everyone, including the party.”

Reacting, the PDP National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Mohammed, said Wike’s support for President Bola Tinubu should not be interpreted as an endorsement of the APC, stressing that the minister’s backing was for Tinubu as President.

Mohammed stated, “I think the issue, or rather the position of the minister to support Tinubu, has been mistaken to mean absolute support for the APC. The minister never said he was going to support the APC. Rather, he said his support is for Tinubu as his President and the person who appointed him to the present position he occupies. So, the feeling that the minister’s gesture of support will be extended to all of them across their states was where they got it wrong. It is important for the APC governors to know that Wike is a force to reckon with, not a force to be rejected.

“It is a complete political misnomer and miscalculation for these governors to assume that the PDP, and indeed the minister, will not field candidates, will not contest against the APC, and will not be able to win against the APC.

“The issue is not even about Wike as a person. It is about how comfortable Nigerians are, particularly with the governors. I am not trying to speak for the President, neither am I trying to speak for the minister. But, in all honesty, the President has given these governors all that is required for them to provide infrastructure and human capital development for the good of the people in their respective states.

“There has been an increase in federal allocations and the issue of financial autonomy for local governments. Yet these governors have muzzled the local government chairmen and refused to allocate or account for the billions of naira accruing to them in their respective states. They have failed to provide good governance and failed to deliver the dividends of democracy.”

PDP National Publicity Secretary said the APC governors were jittery because the PDP had fielded credible candidates capable of defeating them in 2027.

He urged the governors to focus on good governance rather than attacking Wike, noting that INEC’s publication of PDP candidates had proved the party would contest the elections.

Mohammed added, “Now that it is time for elections, they are afraid. The PDP has fielded credible and popular candidates with the capacity and credibility to defeat these APC governors. That is why they are crying wolf where there is none. That is why they are jittery.

“But I can tell you, if truly they are lovers of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and are concerned about the success and victory of their presidential candidate, then I do not see any reason why they would be pushing away a strong political phenomenon like Minister Wike.

“For us, if there is a way we can make the minister rescind his decision not to support our presidential candidate, we would be glad to do that. But we are only respecting his constitutional right to choose whoever he wants to support as a citizen of this country, particularly as an appointee of the President.

“When you compare the records of the minister when he was governor and now that he is a minister, his record is something that cannot be matched by any of these governors. So why are they scared? I will call on them to go back to their respective states, deliver the dividends of democracy, keep the people and account for their stewardship. That is when they can begin to say Wike is not going with us or not.”

On his part, the National Publicity Secretary of the Turaki Interim National Working Committee, Ini Ememobong, said the APC governors and the President created a monster that eventually turned against them by allowing Wike to work for an APC-led government while remaining a PDP member and allegedly acting against the interests of the PDP.

Ememobong stated, “They created a monster, that monster ended up in their belly. And so, the APC governors and the President, who were enjoying the anomaly that Wike constituted, working for an APC government while claiming to be PDP and, obviously, working against the interests of the PDP.

“At some point, they were excited about it, and today it is their turn to play in the belly of the monster. If the President does not intervene and bring this to a stop, he will also end up in the belly of the monster. It is only a matter of time.

“Politics is not just a practice; it is also a field of study. Therefore, practice must follow theory, and there is no theory that can support what is being presented as political practice in Nigeria.”

“When people talk about the Rainbow Coalition, what is it? You belong to a political party. That political party has an ideology and a structure, and it goes from the top to the bottom. There is no ideology called a Rainbow Coalition. It is anti-democratic, and it may lead to the collapse of democracy.”

Efforts by our correspondent to reach the APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, his deputy, Duro Meseko, and the Presidency were unsuccessful, as they did not respond to calls as at the time of filing this report.

content:
Suspected armed herders have ambushed the entourage of the Divisional Police Officer in Ayilamo, Logo Local Government Area of Benue State, killing two police officers.

The latest attack occurred on Monday evening, barely days after suspected herders reportedly killed four policemen and seven residents in the same community.

Sources in the community told our correspondent on Tuesday that the DPO, who had travelled to Makurdi on official duty, was returning to Ayilamo when his entourage was ambushed by the armed assailants.

One of the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the victims were among newly deployed Mobile Police officers in the area.

He said, “At about 6pm on Monday, some newly deployed Mobile Police officers to Ayilamo community were attacked and killed.

“The incident occurred while the officers were on their way from Ayilamo to escort the Divisional Police Officer, who was returning to the community from Makurdi.”

The latest incident came barely four days after suspected armed herders attacked Ayilamo community, killing four police officers and seven residents.

Confirming the latest attack, the spokesperson for the Benue State Police Command, DSP Peter Aondongu, said two officers in the DPO’s entourage were killed.

Aondongu said, “The DPO came to Makurdi to collect some things, and while returning to Ayilamo, he was attacked and lost two of his men in the attack.”

title: EPL to have first-ever 16-day international break from September 21
description:
The Premier League will have its first-ever 16-day international break this season after FIFA merged the traditional September and October windows into a single extended period from September 21 to October 6.
The league will play through Matchweek 5 on September 20 before pausing, with Matchweek 6 r
content:
The Premier League will have its first-ever 16-day international break this season after FIFA merged the traditional September and October windows into a single extended period from September 21 to October 6.

The league will play through Matchweek 5 on September 20 before pausing, with Matchweek 6 resuming on October 10.

During the extended break, European countries will play UEFA Nations League fixtures, while African nations will contest Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, with each country playing two matches. CONCACAF teams will feature in a mixture of Nations League group-stage games and friendlies, while the United States and Mexico, already qualified for the quarter-finals, will play friendlies.

Asian nations will play friendlies in preparation for the Asian Cup in January 2027, following the conclusion of Asian Cup qualifying, while several South American countries are also scheduled to play friendlies.

As retrieved on Wednesday by our correspondent from the EPL website from a September report, previously, there were four nine-day international breaks during the Premier League campaign—in September, October, November and March—with each country playing two matches per window.

However, this season, the “September and October breaks have been merged into one 16-day period, during which countries will play four matches rather than the standard two.”

“With many players in Europe representing countries in Africa and South America, the idea behind the new calendar is to reduce the number of separate periods in which players fly across continents.

“It will also reduce disruption by cutting the number of breaks between the start of the season and the end of the year from three to two,” the Premier League said.

The changes were unanimously approved by the FIFA Council in 2023, with player welfare a factor in the decision.

The breaks can effectively feel longer for Premier League clubs because players return from national-team duty before playing again the following weekend.

“The breaks tend to feel more like two weeks – or three weeks in the case of the new longer window – as players return to clubs and do not play until the following weekend,” the league said.

The November international break will run from November 9 to 17, between Matchweeks 10 and 11, while the final break of the Premier League season will take place from March 22 to 30, between Matchweeks 30 and 31.

In November, European countries will continue in the Nations League with two matches, while AFCON qualification will progress with two more fixtures.

The United States and Mexico will join the other qualified sides in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals, while South American and Asian nations will play friendlies.

The March break will see the start of EURO 2028 qualifying for some countries, alongside UEFA Nations League knockout matches, including the League A quarter-finals and League A, B and C playoffs.

AFCON qualification will continue, while the CONCACAF Nations League final will also be staged. Asian and South American countries will play friendlies during the window.

The Premier League said the international-break system was established in 2002 and first used for qualification for the 2006 FIFA World Cup.

In what became formally known as the “FIFA International Match Calendar”, FIFA introduced fixed periods in the season when clubs were required to make players available for their national teams due to the increasing number of fixtures.

The league also noted that major tournaments such as the FIFA World Cup and continental competitions can take place within FIFA windows, even when they fall during the Premier League off-season.

“When the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) fell between December and January last season, clubs had to release players in a specific window for the tournament, though the Premier League did not take a break,” it said.

There had been discussions about reducing the number of international breaks further, but the current system will remain in place until at least 2030.

“Premier League matches are also not held on a Monday night ahead of an international break or on a Friday night after the break,” the release concluded.

title: Police rescue teenager locked in toilet, arrest Rivers couple

content:
The Rivers State Police Command has arrested a couple for allegedly locking their 15-year-old house help, identified simply as Amaechi, in a toilet at their residence in Abuloma, Port Harcourt City Local Government Area of the state.

The teenager, who hails from Ebonyi State, was reportedly rescued by operatives of the Abuloma Police Division on Monday, September 14, after the landlord raised the alarm over her prolonged absence.

The couple, whose names were withheld, allegedly locked the girl in the toilet for weeks over an undisclosed offence.

A source told our correspondent that while in confinement, the teenager was allegedly fed once a day with leftover food, despite repeatedly pleading for her release.

Another account had it that the girl’s cries attracted the attention of neighbours, who raised the alarm, prompting the police to intervene.

Confirming the incident in a telephone interview with our correspondent on Tuesday, the spokesperson for the Rivers State Police Command, Blessing Agabe, an Assistant Superintendent of Police, said the landlord’s observation led to the girl’s rescue.

Agabe said, “Yes, I can confirm the incident.

“It was the landlord that noticed that the girl had not been coming out of the house for some time. He suspected something and informed the police.

“So our men got there and rescued the girl from the house where she was locked up in the toilet. She was their house help. We have contacted the family of the girl to come to the station.

“The husband and the wife that she was living with as their house help have been arrested. They are with us and investigation is ongoing.”

The police spokesperson added that the teenager would not be returned to the house where she was allegedly confined.

“We asked the family of the girl to come to the station because the girl will not return to the house she was picked up from,” she said.

Asked whether the couple would be arraigned, Agabe said, “Well, for now, investigation is ongoing.”

content:
A man identified as Adejuwon Adekunle, aka Asa, has been shot dead by gunmen near a recreation centre in the Dele Yes Sir community, Osogbo, Osun State.

Adekunle was reportedly attacked between 1:30am and 2am on Tuesday by yet-to-be-identified assailants, who allegedly traced him to the area.

The circumstances surrounding the killing remained unclear as of the time of filing this report.

However, the Osun State Police Command said preliminary findings suggested that the incident might be cult-related, assuring that investigation had commenced to unravel the circumstances surrounding the killing.

The command’s spokesperson, Abiodun Ojelabi, who confirmed the incident in a telephone interview with our correspondent on Tuesday, said the victim was rushed to a hospital after he was shot but was pronounced dead on arrival.

Ojelabi said, “What happened in Dele Yes Sir is suspected to be a cult-related attack. The incident occurred around 2am on Tuesday.

“We got information that some armed men went to the area and started shooting sporadically. One Adejuwon Adekunle, aka Asa, was shot and rushed to the hospital, where he was confirmed dead on arrival. His body was deposited at the morgue.

“The Commissioner of Police has directed that the case be transferred to the Criminal Investigation Department for a more discreet investigation. We have not made any arrest regarding the incident.”

Meanwhile, the command said some persons had been invited and interrogated in connection with the killing of an Accord Party chieftain, Olalekan Oyeyemi, popularly known as Emir Ajagungbade, in Ile-Ife on Sunday.

Ojelabi, however, declined to disclose the identities of those invited for questioning.

He said, “No arrest has been made yet. Some persons were invited by our operatives at the Criminal Investigation Department, and they were interrogated about the incident.”

PUNCH Metro reports that the police had recovered another corpse within the precinct of the Mayfair Motor Park, Ile-Ife, bringing to two the number of persons reportedly killed in the shooting incident at the park.

The development came as the remains of Oyeyemi were interred at his newly completed residence in the Agunbelewo area of Osogbo on Monday, according to traditional rites.

PUNCH Online reports that Oyeyemi was shot dead on Sunday during a clash involving him and a group led by another leader of the National Union of Road Transport Workers, identified by his nickname, Sibi, at the Mayfair Motor Park.

A video circulating on social media showed Oyeyemi lying face down in a pool of blood inside a vehicle after the incident.

Nigeria’s Flamingos will use the second WAFU B U-17 Girls Tournament in Ivory Coast as a springboard for their FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup campaign, with coach Hakeem Busari targeting the title before heading to Morocco.

The Flamingos arrived in Ivory Coast on Monday for the regional tournament and will now face Niger Republic on Wednesday after the withdrawal of Benin Republic’s U-17 team.

The change means Nigeria will no longer face Ghana’s Princesses in their opening game, with the much-anticipated clash now scheduled for Saturday.

“This is the kind of tournament we want to win and build on it for the task ahead, which is the World Cup,” Busari said ahead of their opening match against Niger Republic.

Busari selected 20 players for the tournament, which provides an important preparatory platform for Nigeria and Ghana, two of Africa’s four representatives at this year’s FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

Kenya and Zambia are the continent’s other representatives.

The 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup will be held in Morocco from October 17 to November 8.

Nigeria have been drawn in Group B alongside North Korea, Puerto Rico and Poland, while Ghana are in Group C with Canada, Brazil and Norway.

title: Why Premier League teams failed to sign Osimhen – Cole
description:
Former Manchester United striker Andy Cole says several factors beyond transfer fees and salaries may have prevented Premier League clubs from signing Victor Osimhen.
Osimhen has been linked with Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea in recent years, but none of the clubs completed a dea
content:
Former Manchester United striker Andy Cole says several factors beyond transfer fees and salaries may have prevented Premier League clubs from signing Victor Osimhen.

Osimhen has been linked with Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea in recent years, but none of the clubs completed a deal for the Nigeria international.

Speaking to GOAL, Cole said Osimhen has the quality to succeed in the Premier League but suggested that transfers involve several considerations.

“He does. He scores goals. He scored goals in Italy and he’s scoring goals in Turkey as well,” Cole said.

“But, you know, it depends. There are many different factors in signing a player from a respective country. It’s not all about just the salary or the transfer fee. There could be many different things that go on.

“If he does come to the Premier League, which I think he will be very good at, you never know who he’ll go to.”

Osimhen began his European career with Wolfsburg before making his breakthrough during a loan spell at Belgian side Charleroi. He later joined Lille and then Napoli, where he helped the club win the Serie A title in the 2022/23 season.

The striker scored 31 goals that season and has continued to impress since moving to Galatasaray, where he has scored 65 goals in 78 appearances.

His performances have continued to attract interest from Premier League clubs, particularly Manchester United.

Former United defender Patrice Evra recently backed the club to sign Osimhen, describing him as the type of striker United need.

“I think Osimhen is the best. He’s a perfect example,” Evra told GOAL.

Former France international Louis Saha has also urged United to pursue the 27-year-old, highlighting his goalscoring record, Champions League experience and success with Napoli and Galatasaray.

Despite the recommendations from former United players, the club have not made a move for Osimhen and have instead signed Benjamin Sesko as their main out-and-out striker.

Osimhen remains under contract at Galatasaray, although Premier League interest could return in future transfer windows.

title: Nigeria’s capital challenge is finding bankable opportunities
description:
Nigeria does not lack capital, but rather a sufficient volume of investable, bankable opportunities capable of attracting and absorbing available funds, experts at the 2026 Chief Executive Officer Forum of the UN Global Compact Network Nigeria have stated.
The closed-door forum, held in Lagos under
content:
Nigeria does not lack capital, but rather a sufficient volume of investable, bankable opportunities capable of attracting and absorbing available funds, experts at the 2026 Chief Executive Officer Forum of the UN Global Compact Network Nigeria have stated.

The closed-door forum, held in Lagos under the theme “Financing a Dignified Future: Aligning Capital, Policy and Business Action,” brought together chief executives, policymakers, financiers, and development partners to examine how capital, policy, and enterprise can drive economic productivity.

In her opening address, the CEO and Executive Director of UN Global Compact Network Nigeria, Naomi Nwokolo, urged business leaders to shift focus from longstanding constraints toward immediate, actionable solutions that foster long-term competitiveness, living wages, and sustainable growth.

Contributing to the dialogue, the Director-General of the Northwest Governors Forum, Maryam Musa Yahaya, stressed that state governments must actively engage investors to resolve specific structural bottlenecks, including power, regulatory friction, and security concerns.

Highlighting a practical model, Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, outlined his administration’s 10-year development plan aimed at bolstering policy predictability, improving geophysical data, and boosting internally generated revenue from N90m to roughly N45bn monthly.

Addressing financial access, the Deputy Managing Director of First Bank of Nigeria, Ini Ebong, stated that financial inclusion must be treated as critical infrastructure rather than corporate social responsibility, noting that the broader constraint remains the capacity of small businesses to become financeable through proper record-keeping and corporate governance.

On institutional capital deployment, the Group Chief Operating Officer of Custodian Investment, Adeniyi Falade, revealed that out of the pension industry’s N32tn asset pool, less than three per cent is allocated to infrastructure due to a scarcity of properly structured, bankable projects.

Similarly, the Managing Director of Sahara Power Group, Anthony Youdeowei, noted that addressing energy deficits requires substantial capital for distribution infrastructure alongside clear tariff frameworks to ensure investor returns.

Providing an international trade perspective, the Deputy High Commissioner of Canada to Nigeria, Carlos Rojas-Arbulú, stated that while bilateral merchandise trade between both nations has surpassed $3bn, global capital remains highly selective, prioritising transparent data and bankable feasibility studies over general market potential.

title: Ex-labour leader seeks oil buffer to stabilise petrol prices
description:

A former National Vice President of the Petroleum and Nat
content:
Nigeria needs a mechanism to absorb exceptional increases in global oil prices while the government tackles the structural costs of petrol production and distribution, veteran labour leader and oil and gas practitioner Mustapha Wali has said.

A former National Vice President of the Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, Wali, in a non-partisan policy document, ‘Beyond Petroleum Subsidy: A Petroleum Price Moderator and Downstream Transformation Framework for Nigeria,’ made available to journalists in Kano on Tuesday, proposed the establishment of a petroleum price moderator backed by a ring-fenced stabilisation reserve.

He argued that Nigeria’s recurring petrol price crisis could not be sustainably addressed by restoring the old subsidy regime or relying on ad hoc government interventions whenever pump prices became politically or economically difficult.

The proposed reserve, he said, would accumulate funds when international petroleum prices were favourable and deploy them when prices rose beyond predetermined thresholds.

“This is not a return to the old subsidy regime. It is a counter-cyclical stabilisation mechanism designed to protect consumers from exceptional shocks while Nigeria tackles the structural causes of high petroleum costs,” he said.

Wali called for a forensic review of the existing petroleum pricing template covering crude supply, refining, freight, foreign exchange, financing, pipelines, storage, depots, transportation and distribution.

According to him, the review should distinguish between genuinely unavoidable costs and those that are excessive, reducible, unnecessary or capable of being addressed through regulation.

He also proposed a predictable system under which qualified domestic refineries would have clearly defined access to crude, covering allocation, pricing, delivery obligations, quality standards, measurement, dispute resolution and penalties for non-performance.

“Although domestic crude oil is not free, local supply can eliminate some freight, handling and logistics costs, with such savings reflected transparently in the commercial structure,” Wali said.

Beyond crude supply and refining, he identified the country’s petroleum infrastructure deficit as another cost driver. He proposed transforming the Nigerian Pipeline and Storage Company Limited into a professionally managed national petroleum infrastructure operator and opening strategic infrastructure to users on transparent and non-discriminatory terms.

He also called for independent technical and commercial assessments of the refineries owned by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited to determine which facilities could still be economically rehabilitated.

Facilities found viable, he said, should be opened to partnerships involving competent private investors, international refinery operators, technical firms, infrastructure investors and development finance institutions.

Wali also urged international oil companies and upstream producers to participate more directly in Nigeria’s downstream transformation through investments in refinery rehabilitation, crude supply, storage, pipelines, financing, technology and other infrastructure.

He proposed that once the stabilisation reserve accumulates beyond an agreed threshold, part of it could be deployed as repayable financing for commercially viable downstream projects, including pipelines, storage facilities, depots, LPG projects, strategic petroleum reserves, terminals and refinery rehabilitation.

“This way, Nigeria will not simply spend money to reduce today’s petrol price. We will invest in reducing tomorrow’s petroleum cost,” he said.

Wali said the long-term objective should be to move Nigeria away from dependence on imported petroleum products and develop the country into a regional refining and supply hub for West Africa.

He stressed that his proposal was not designed to advance the interest of any political party or presidential candidate, saying the framework had been circulated for consideration by political leaders and national policymakers ahead of the 2027 elections.

He challenged presidential candidates to explain how they intended to achieve sustainable petrol pricing and downstream industrialisation without returning to subsidy or relying on temporary political interventions.

“What is your sustainable petroleum pricing and downstream industrialisation model for Nigeria beyond subsidy and short-term political interventions?” he asked.

title: Messi Named In Argentina Squad For Farewell Match Against Benin
description: Lionel Messi was on Tuesday named in Argentina’s squad for a friendly against Benin on October 6, a match that will serve as his farewell appearance after announcing his international retirement last month.The 39-year-old said in August he was retiring from Argentina duty after a two-decade in
content:
Lionel Messi was on Tuesday named in Argentina’s squad for a friendly against Benin on October 6, a match that will serve as his farewell appearance after announcing his international retirement last month.

The 39-year-old said in August he was retiring from Argentina duty after a two-decade international career that included winning the 2022 World Cup and Copa America triumphs in 2021 and 2024.

“We made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves on October 6 here in Argentina,” said Argentine FA president Claudio Tapia.

The match against Benin will take place at River Plate’s Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. Tapia has also invited all of Argentina’s 2022 World Cup winners to join Messi for the occasion.

Argentina begin a series of three friendlies against Bolivia on September 30 in Cordoba — their first match since losing the World Cup final to Spain — before taking on Burkina Faso in Buenos Aires on October 3.

Messi has been included in the squad for the third match against Benin, when he is expected to make his 208th and final appearance for the national team. He is Argentina’s all-time record scorer with 125 goals.

Last month FIFA ordered Argentina to play their next home match with capacity reduced to 50 percent for breaches of its disciplinary code relating to using a sports event for making demonstrations of a non-sporting nature.

After Argentina beat England 2-1 in a tense World Cup semi-final in July, several players held up a banner saying: “The Falklands are Argentine”.

The friendlies are also expected to count towards suspensions handed down following incidents after Argentina’s World Cup final defeat by Spain.

Midfielder Leandro Paredes received a 10-match ban, while defender Nahuel Molina was suspended for seven games and Thiago Almada for one.
